News.title: Will the hot weather return? What the Met Office says about another heatwave as UK temperatures drop
News.content:
THE mercury has dropped sharply since last week’s 38.1C, leaving the UK a cooler, wetter place.

But the Met Office says hot spells could still return this summer, raising the prospect of the year’s sixth heatwave.



Will the hot weather return?

From August 23 to September 1, the Met Office expects a largely dry and settled start as a ridge of high pressure builds, with a few showers in the far north and possibly the far southeast.

Conditions look set to turn increasingly unsettled through next week as low pressure takes charge and squeezes that ridge away to the northeast.



Most areas are expected to see some showers or heavy rain, particularly towards the end of next week, and there’s a risk of wind, hail and thunder.

Temperatures are forecast to sit near or just below average, with some chilly nights at first, but brief warm and humid spells are still possible, particularly in the south.



But things could change from September 1, with the forecaster raising the prospect of another heatwave.

The Met Office said: “As we move into the start of meteorological autumn, signals for the prevailing weather patterns affecting the UK are weak, thus something close to the climatological norm is most likely.

“This means a broad northwest-southeast split in conditions, with higher pressure becoming centred close to the south of the UK and lower pressure towards the north and northwest.

“The north and northwest will probably see the lion’s share of the rain and any strong winds, whilst the south and southeast will probably see the driest and sunniest weather.



“Temperatures are likely to be above average overall.

“There is a chance that late season hot spells or heatwaves develop, especially in the south.”

This would follow the fifth heatwave of a record-breaking summer, which brought highs of 38.1C in Kew Gardens, London, on Thursday last week – the hottest day of the year so far.

What is the weather forecast this week?

The Met Office said today will be cloudy for much of the UK, with outbreaks of rain mainly in the west and heavier bursts across northern Scotland.

Sunny spells are expected to develop from the west, with showers hitting Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England, and it will feel slightly cooler overall.



Sunshine is predicted to linger in the far south this evening before cloud thickens from the west, bringing drizzle to much of England and Wales.

Rain will clear the far southeast on Wednesday, with sunny spells developing for the most part.

Heavy, persistent showers across Scotland will spread more widely through the day with thunder possible in places.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A northerly wind will develop between Thursday and Saturday, dragging temperatures below average.

Thundery showers are forecast for Thursday and Friday, before it turns brighter and drier on Saturday.

News.title: I was UK’s sickest child, allergic to food, hooked up to oxygen with 4 ops by six…shock truth emerged after mum’s arrest
News.content:
EVERYONE thought she was the perfect mum – not least, Lisa Hayden-Johnson herself.

She tirelessly devoted her life to her young son, Matthew – dubbed “Britain’s Sickest Child” – who was allergic to almost every food, fed through a tube and needed an oxygen tank, wheelchair and a cocktail of drugs for a string of illnesses including diabetes, cerebral palsy and cystic fibrosis.



With his cherubic looks, he won the nation’s hearts as he coped with his burden with a winsome smile. And everyone admired Lisa’s selfless nature. Their story featured in newspaper and magazine articles and they were invited onto TV, with Matthew receiving a prestigious bravery award from Queen Camilla, when she was the Duchess of Cornwall, and meeting then Prime Minister, Tony Blair.

Lisa sought medical help 325 times for her son before he was six. He underwent nine general anaesthetics and had four invasive operations.

But it was all a charade – and the only person making Matthew ill was his mother.



Lisa was diagnosed with the rare condition Munchausen by Proxy (now known as Fabrication Induced Illness) – a form of abuse in which an individual, usually the mother, feigns, exaggerates or induces illness in her own child in order to gain attention and sympathy.

In 2010, she was convicted of child cruelty and found herself being described in her local newspaper as “Britain’s most evil mother”.

In an exclusive interview with The Sun, ahead of a new Channel 4 documentary, Matthew Johnson and sister Laura speak out for the first time on how their mother’s lies damaged their lives.

“It does concern me that her actions could have killed me but then I also feel very blessed and lucky that I managed to move on and start anew and be just like any other fit and healthy person who can look after themselves,” says Matthew, now 25. “There’s nothing impairing me from having that life.

“It took me a long time to properly understand what my mum had done because I was so young, but I think also I wanted to avoid the reality of what had happened.



“I felt the more I understood it, the more it would take me away from having a mum. So, it wasn’t something I wanted to explore. I only really addressed that when I was older.”

Remarkably, 16 years on, Lisa refuses to accept she did wrong and insists she was only doing the best for Matthew.

Lisa talks on camera for the first time, since her release from prison, in the three-part documentary, Love You To Death, along with her two children, Matthew and Laura Johnson.

“The only thing I was guilty of was putting my son first and fighting his battle. And I don’t regret that,” she says.

Matthew was born prematurely in 2001 and had to remain in Torbay Hospital for six months before being welcomed into the family home in the seaside town of Brixham, Devon.



Concerned that he was not “hitting his milestones”, Lisa took to focussing almost all her attention on him receiving the right medical help, while her husband, Christopher went to work. Matthew’s besotted two-year-old sister, Laura, was keen to help look after her little brother in any way she could.

Matthew’s paediatrician, Dr Stella Imong, who worked at Torbay Hospital for many years, says: “Most premature babies recover very quickly, but not Matthew. He would be in and out of the ward all the time. He was almost a permanent resident. He had his own consultant, Dr John Broomhall.”

Having told medics that she was a qualified nurse, the hospital agreed to let Lisa administer his oxygen and food at home and arranged weekly deliveries of various drugs to the house.



“She could be quite demanding,” recalls Stella. “She knew exactly what she wanted for Matthew. A lot of people on the ward had concerns about her.”

Suspicions grew as X-rays and tests for alleged swallowing problems showed nothing amiss. Irritated by what she saw as a lack of improvement, Lisa said she was taking Matthew to Great Ormond Street.

“I never asked what was wrong with me, because I was so young,” says Matthew. “I only understood I was different to other children and I was under the assumption that everything was happening for a reason.”

Matthew’s plight attracted the attention of the local newspaper and TV news who published stories about him having to drag an oxygen tank behind him on a trolley, regularly needed a wheelchair and how Lisa tirelessly liquidised his food and arranged his drugs.

“It was weird because he wasn’t always using his wheelchair or the oxygen tank when we went out,” says Laura, now 27.



Matthew was put forward for a Children of Courage Award, receiving his medal from Camilla at Westminster Abbey and having his picture taken outside 10 Downing Street with Tony Blair.

At a dinner for the Children of Courage, the family was delighted to be sitting with Simon Cowell, who invited them all to watch a recording of The X Factor.

Lisa, Christopher, Laura and Matthew were also invited onto the couch on GMTV. Here, Lisa told how Matthew couldn’t eat treats like chocolate and crisps and he was very good about it.



Laura was puzzled. “That wasn’t true, because at home we would have ice-cream and chocolate. Just normal things. I was so confused,” she says.

Meanwhile, concerned medics went to the police with their concerns. Matthew’s medical records were handed over – three box loads.

DS Steve Blair of Devon and Cornwall Police, together with a health professional and a social worker, found Lisa had been giving false readings of Matthew’s blood sugar levels for diabetes at home and lied to Torbay Hospital about advice Great Ormond Street had given her.

When Dr Broomhall insisted that they take Matthew off medication, Lisa stormed out. Things were beginning to unravel.

Lisa then sensationally claimed to have been raped by a motorcyclist – even cutting her own face. After police could find no evidence of an attack, she admitted to having made it up – even now attempting to justify her lies.



“I’ve had to come to terms with the fact that it happened in my head and not in real life,” she said.

In 2007 she was arrested on suspicion of harming Matthew. She was found to have lied about her medical qualification and a search of the house revealed box after box of unused medication which was still being ordered every week.

A cupboard was full of glucose powder that police believe she added to Matthew’s urine samples to trick doctors into believing he had diabetes.



There were also family pictures of days out and a free cruise – with Matthew happily playing and tucking into a roast dinner, burgers and orange squash.

It is estimated that the various benefits she claimed for Matthew made her £200,000.

On questioning, it became evident that Christopher was in the dark about what had been going on and believed Lisa was doing the best she could for their ‘sick’ son.

Following Lisa’s arrest, Matthew was moved into temporary foster care. He was gradually taken off all medication and began to eat and breathe like any other healthy child.

“She had constrained his life so much that it was equivalent, really, to physical abuse,” says Stella.



“With Matthew in care, it was just me and dad for a while,” says Laura. “The social worker explained to us that mum had hurt Matthew. I remember being angry at them. But then they started explaining that Matthew wasn’t ill and it was all a lie.

“My dad was so heartbroken. It wasn’t until she actually got arrested that I ever heard my dad speaking negatively about her. He would say things like, ‘She’s ruined your lives,’ ‘She nearly killed your brother.’ That was a shock because I had grown up witnessing such amazing love between them. Now it was hate.”

Christopher and his two children moved away from the area and settled in Sheffield. And although it was a welcome fresh start for Matthew, Laura missed her friends and felt like she didn’t fit in.



“Sometimes I feel like my life started when I moved to Sheffield,” says Matthew. “Although I was struggling with the loss of my mum being around, it felt like a new life. I could do things. It was nice to have a fresh slate and just be like a normal kid.”

At her trial, Lisa, then 35, pleaded guilty and was given a three-year and three-month sentence for child cruelty and perverting the course of justice between 2001 and 2007. She was released in 2011, having served 19 months.

Now, she says she pled guilty just so that people would leave her alone and that she did no wrong.



When she came out of prison, she requested to see her children and they met up with her for an hour, with a social worker, despite Christopher wanting to break all contact with her.

“I must have been 11 or 12 and I ran into her arms and gave her a hug,” Matthew remembers. “I just wanted to see my mum again and I felt that way for quite a few years afterwards.”

More meetings followed then, when Laura was 16, and feeling in need of a more permanent mum in her life, she moved back in with her for a time.

“Life was amazing with her at first,” she says. “I was just so grateful to have her in my life. I wasn’t thinking too much about what she had done in the past.”

But, to her alarm, her mum then became unwell and Laura found herself having to push her around in a wheelchair.



“It was like I was her carer,” she says. “She also had what I called blips, where she regressed into a five-year old, watching Peppa Pig and self-harming herself, before snapping out of it, seemingly unaware of what she was doing.

“When I moved out, all her blipping magically disappeared and she no longer needed a wheelchair.”

Matthew and Laura have now cut all ties with their mother.

“Her mindset hasn’t shifted in the two decades that have passed,” says Matthew. “She still thinks she never did anything wrong. She clearly has no remorse or understanding of what she’s done.”

“I have mixed emotions about her now – part anger, part sympathy,” says Laura. “I sympathise that she’s very clearly got something going on mentally but I still feel angry that she could do those things. I think that at some point you have to take accountability for what you have done. But she isn’t going to and it would be too damaging to us both if we were to build a relationship again only to see it break once more.”



Today, Laura, lives happily with her partner of seven years and works in childcare.

“It’s something I’m really passionate about and I think I can benefit it in being able to spot signs a bit easier,” she smiles.

Matthew is also happy and contented.

“I have a job in admin and I live on my own in a house in Chesterfield, so I’m not too far from Sheffield where we moved,” he says. “I’ve got a great circle of friends that have been really supportive, as well as family members, so we’re both definitely in a good place.”

“I’ve accepted that my mum is who she he and isn’t going to be able to change. I forgive her for what she’s done. I don’t wish her any ill health, and I just hope that she can live the rest of her life in peace as much as we both deserve to.”



Love You To Death, Channel 4, Wednesday 19 August

News.title: Mum ‘found photo of son, 14, with teacher accused of having sex with him 30 times after she kept calling family home’
News.content:
'PAEDO' MISS Mum ‘found photo of son, 14, with teacher accused of having sex with him 30 times after she kept calling family home’

A MUM found a photo of her son with a female teacher accused of having sex with him up to 30 times, a court heard.

Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, allegedly abused two boys at Christ’s College in Finchley, North London when they were aged 14 and 15 in the 1980s.



The teacher – then aged 25 – allegedly “engaged in flirtatious conduct” with the pupils and “engaged in sexual relationships with them both”.

Harrow Crown Court heard the mum of the 14-year-old boy tore up a picture of her son with Bowen taken in a photobooth.



She told jurors: “They were taken in a photobooth. A little black and white picture. Their heads were pushed together, this woman and my son.

“I was so angry I tore them up. I’m still angry all these years because that was evidence.”

The mum also told the court she discovered her son was “involved” with Bowen after they were seen walking together in London.

She said she sent him away for two weeks but the teacher just “kept ringing the phone”.

The mum told how she got Bowen’s phone number and told her she “knew she was having an affair with my son and wanted it to stop”.

Giving evidence previously, the boy told jurors he slept with Bowen “about 20 or 30 times”.



He also denied being a “fantasist” who invented the allegations – branding the suggestion “quite insulting”.

In a police interview, the boy said Bowen would dress in a “sexually provocative” way while teaching chemistry at the all-boys’ school.

He described her outfits as “tight Levi’s jeans and black skinny pants that you could see everything in, and a black mini skirt”.



The boy also told police how on one occasion, the boys were looking at a porn magazine when Bowen took it from them.

Jurors heard he expected her to confiscate it but she instead “pointed to an image of a naked woman” and said “that’s what my p***y looks like”.

Bowen later told the boy she was leaving the UK to stay at a kibbutz in Israel, the court heard.

The boy first disclosed the alleged abuse to a partner, who told him to go to police.

When Bowen was interviewed in 2015, she claimed he was a “bit of a nuisance” and “besotted” with her.



Jurors heard she described the sexual relationship claims as “just pure fantasy”.

As a result of the allegations, Bowen faced a Teaching Regulation Authority hearing in 2022.

The teacher is also accused of letting the second boy touch her breasts and kiss her during lunch at a cafe near the school.



The court heard he later read about the TRA hearing online and came forward after encouragement from his wife and family.

He claimed he was “goaded” by other boys at the school into kissing “young and attractive” Bowen.

The pupil also remembered touching her breasts and putting his hand near her crotch – to which “she would not react negatively”, it was said.

In his police interview, he said Bowen was “possibly the hottest teacher in our school”.

He added: “‘She was young, she was pretty. She had long straight blonde hair. She had nice eyes.



‘She walked around in a Levi 501 t-shirt. You know I said not good language, but she would walk around with her t*ts sticking out.

‘I think she knew it. She had that level of confidence. Some people like that, want that, appreciate it.

‘But she never really caught my eye. I was a bit of a goth. I liked girls with dark hair and she wasn’t.

‘People would always have conversations. ‘Who’s the fittest teacher? Who would you want to be with the most?’ And she was always at the top of everyone’s list.”

Bowen denies eight counts of indecent assault.



The trial continues.

News.title: Warning over ‘BOTULISM outbreak’ in popular UK park as water may contain deadly bacteria than can cause paralysis
News.content:
AUTHORITIES are investigating reports of a life-threatening toxin in a major UK city park.

Concerned residents reported a potential outbreak of deadly bacteria in a lake, with local wildlife reportedly falling sick.



Bristol City Council has confirmed that it is looking into the potential outbreak of conditions associated with boutlism at the lake in St George’s Park.

A spokesperson for the council said: “We are aware of reports concerning suspected botulism in the lake at St George Park and are actively investigating them.”



The council has urged members of the public not to touch injured animals in the area and to steer clear of the lake.

Members of the public have also been advised to avoid people and dogs who have come into contact with the water.

Botulism is caused by a paralysing neurotoxin produced by Clostridium botulinum bacteria.

Ingestion of this toxin or the bacteria which produces it can cause animals and humans to become sick.

While transmission between animals and people is rare, precautions should still be taken.

The illness most often affects humans via contaminated food.



According to the NHS, Botulism can be life-threatening and requires immediate treatment in hospital.

The council has reminds people in the area no to touch sick, injured, or dead animals near the lake and keep their own dogs on a lead.

Dog owners should also make sure their pet does not enter the water, with residents advised to avoid contact with the lake where possible.

Members of the public have also been advised not to feed on wild birds in the area.

If you find a sick or dead bird, phone Bristol City Council on 0117 922 000 or report a problem in a park by visiting the website.



A resident told BristolLive: “Bath Swan Rescue are doing an incredible job responding to the outbreak, voluntarily rescuing and caring for affected wildlife.

“I have raised concerns with Bristol City Council and other relevant organisations, including the Animal Health Team and RSPCA.

Locals shared concerns over a broken aerator in the lake, which they are concerned “could potentially be contributing to environmental conditions associated with botulism”.

“I appreciate that this cannot be assumed to be the cause of the outbreak, but given the circumstances, many residents feel that it warrants urgent investigation,” the resident added.

News.title: Four people ‘in difficulty’ in sea on UK beach – as air ambulance and emergency crews swoop on scene
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BEACH HORROR Four people ‘in difficulty’ in sea on UK beach – as air ambulance and emergency crews swoop on scene

EMERGENCY crews have descended upon a popular beach after four people got into difficulty in the sea.

Pictures showed emergency services, including seven ambulances and two helicopters, swoop on Shoreham, West Sussex, this afternoon.



Shocked locals described hearing “lots of sirens” as crews descended upon the popular seafront.

Roger Pettitt, who lives in nearby Mile Oak, said his daughter saw two helicopters landing at the port.



He told The Argus: “A yellow helicopter landed by the lifeboat station.

“There’s loads of police, loads of ambulances, fire engines. A lot of sirens.”



South East Coast Ambulance Service confirmed it was called to reports of four people in need of medical attention near Shoreham Harbour.

A spokesperson said: “We were called shortly after 3pm and have a number of ambulance resources at the scene.



“We have no further information to share at this time but will provide updates as soon as possible.”

Sussex Police said: “Emergency services are currently responding to reports of four people in difficulty in the water close to Shoreham Fort.

“A section of the A259 in Shoreham has been closed as the incident remains ongoing, and we’re urging the public to stay clear of the area in the meantime.



“We will provide more information as soon as we are able to.”

Lifeboat crews were launched at about 2.50pm, according to an RNLI spokesperson.

Two additional boats were also sent out roughly ten minutes later.

HM Coastguard added: “HM Coastguard responded to an incident reported at Shoreham at about 2.45pm on 18 August.

“An HM Coastguard helicopter was sent as well as Littlehampton, Shoreham and Newhaven Coastguard Rescue Teams, and an RNLI lifeboat from Shoreham.



“Sussex Police and South East Coast Ambulance Service also attended.”

Labour MP for East Worthing and Shoreham Tom Rutland said: “Please stay clear of the area around Shoreham Fort and Kingston Beach as emergency services respond to reports of several people in difficulty in the water there.

“A section of the A259 in Shoreham has been closed as the incident remains ongoing.”

News.title: Mum-of-three, 31, drowns after jumping into river to save son, 7, while on family fishing trip
News.content:
A HEROIC mother drowned after jumping into a river to save her son.

The tragedy unfolded on August 16 during a family fishing trip to Des Plaines River at Independence Grove Forest Preserve, Illinois.



Angelina Khalimendik, 31, jumped into the river after her 7-year-old son was swept up by the water.

She helped her son reach safety by passing him to a family member, but officials say she slipped underwater.



Khalimendik was pulled out of the water by people nearby and a family member before emergency services arrived at the scene.

Paramedics performed CPR on her before she was taken to Advocate Condell Medical Center.

READ MORE WORLD NEWS BOAT TRAGEDY 'Drunk' grandfather who crashed boat that killed his two grandkids is charged



However she had already swallowed too much water and was later pronounced dead.

The Lake County Coroner’s office confirmed that Khalimendik’s death was “consistent with drowning.”



Khalimendik’s family returned to the forest preserve on Monday, seeking what they hoped would be closure.

Khalimendik’s husband said his wife was a passionate and devoted mother, and that he will remember her for the care and dedication she showed her children.

She leaves behind her husband, an 11-year-old daughter and two sons, nine and seven.

Ron Davis, Lake County Forest Preserves’ police chief: “We are deeply saddened by the tragic death in the Des Plaines River.

“Our thoughts are with the victim’s family and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.”



Khalimendik’s death followed recent “storms and torrential rains” in the area.

Davis said: “These bodies of water are flooded with not only extra water, but debris, fallen trees, branches, rocks, other things that are under the surface.

“There’s nothing to indicate this was anything more than a tragic accident.”

News.title: Police chief among four arrested in fraud and bribery probe as corruption squad swoops on cop HQ
News.content:
FRAUD PROBE Police chief among four arrested in fraud and bribery probe as corruption squad swoops on cop HQ

THE LEADER of the rank and file Police Federation staff association was one of four senior officials arrested today.

City of London Police investigating allegations of fraud and bribery swooped on the Fed’s offices at Leatherhead, Surrey, this morning.

National chair Tiff Lynch – a serving Leicestershire officer – was arrested along with the Fed’s General Secretary John Partington, a Met cop.

It is understood that a senior female lawyer and a male financial executive working for the Federation – which represents 145,000 officers in England and Wales – were also held during the raid.





The arrests were described as a “significant development” in the City police probe into the Fed’s former CEO Makund Krishna, who was paid more than £700,000 a year with bonuses.

Mr Krishna, 46, was arrested in March on suspicion of fraud by abuse of position along with two other senior Fed officials, aged 51 and 55, in coordinated raids.

The men were all arrested at their homes and bailed.

Former management consultant Mr Makund later had his contract terminated. He has denied any wrong-doing.

City of London Police confirmed they had made further arrests today but declined to name the individuals held under normal protocols.

The force said in a statement: “The City of London Police Domestic Corruption Unit (DCU) have today made four further arrests in relation to an ongoing investigation involving the Police Federation of England and Wales (PFEW).

“The arrests are the latest development in a significant investigation into allegations of fraud and bribery, following three arrests carried out earlier this year (March 2026).

“On Tuesday 18 August, DCU officers arrested four people at an address in Leatherhead, Surrey, as part of an investigation into suspected fraud and bribery offences.



“Those arrested were two men, aged in their 40s and 50s, and two women in their 50s.

“Two of the individuals are serving police officers.

“They were all taken to a police station where they will be questioned in due course.”

It is understood City cops searched offices and seized computers and phones during the swoop today.

Detective Superintendent Jim Halkett, of the City of London Police Domestic Corruption Unit, said: “Our investigation continues to make significant progress, with officers working through a number of lines of enquiry to establish the full facts and circumstances surrounding this case.



“We would like to thank everyone who has already come forward with information.

“This has been valuable and continues to play an important role in helping us move our enquiries forward.

“This remains a complex and high-profile investigation, and we recognise the public and media interest in it.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Federation declined to comment on the arrests.

A spokesperson said: “We will not be commenting at this stage.”

News.title: Popular advent calendar sold in Superdrug and The Range is recalled over chemical that can ‘damage reproductive systems’
News.content:
A POPULAR advent calendar inspired by a viral toy has been urgently recalled for presenting a serious chemical risk.

Shoppers have been urged to stop using the product immediately and to keep the advent calendar out of the reach of children.



Shoppers have been urged to stop using the MESOLAB Leaper Cute Animal Advent Calendar immediately after it was found to contain excess chemical quantities.

The Labubu-themed calendar was widely sold by Superdrug, The Range, Debenhams and Groupon during the run-up to Christmas last year.



Inside one of the 24 doors, the orange character contains excess volumes of Bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) – a colourless, odourless synthetic liquid chemical used in children’s toys.

When found in excess quantities, phthalates can cause harm to the health of children, and has the potential to damage the reproductive system.

The product has therefore been recalled from end users by MESOLAB, a third-party distributor of gifts and novelty items.

Customers who have purchased the advent calendars have been advised to stop using the product immediately and to keep out the reach of children.

Information of the recall further specifies that affected consumers have been contacted directly.

The Santa-themed advent calendar features 24 collectible, multicoloured mini monster figures inside.



As the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) has not identified a specific batch, it is assumed that every advent calendar is affected by the recall.

Under consumer law in the UK, it is a legal right to receive a full cash refund for any recalled products, with shoppers recommended to follow OPSS guidance to organise this.

News.title: London St Pancras - live: Evacuation as 'loud bang' heard near King's Cross
News.content:
London St Pancras train station was evacuated this afternoon as emergency services responded to an incident involving an unattended vehicle near King's Cross

London St Pancras train station was evacuated while emergency services dealt with an unattended vehicle nearby.

East Midlands Railway said passengers were asked to leave the station, while TfL closed the main and north entrances to King’s Cross St Pancras Underground station at the request of the Metropolitan Police.

The Met has since confirmed a controlled explosion was carried out and the vehicle was declared non-suspicious. Witnesses reported hearing a loud bang in the area.

King’s Cross St Pancras Underground station has now fully reopened, although police continue to deal with the scene nearby and disruption remains in the area.

News.title: Met Office names areas facing lightning and hail on Wednesday – 33 counties at risk
News.content:
Met Office names areas facing lightning and hail on Wednesday – 33 counties at risk

Heavy rain and thunder is coming to some parts of the UK within hours, and Met Office weather forecasters even say lightning and hail are possible too

UK weather: Met Office forecasts rain sweeping in

Some parts of the UK face thundery rain, lightning and possibly even hail on Wednesday, the Met Office has said.

‌



Temperatures have dropped into the mid to low-20s across the board following last week's record-breaking 38C heat, with the scorching weather now making way for downpours in some regions.

‌



The Met Office says rain could impact several regions in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland tomorrow - although the heaviest downpours are expected in Scotland and Northern Ireland - where lightning and hail are also on the cards.

‌



Speaking in this afternoon's Met Office video forecast, meteorologist Rachel Davis said for tomorrow morning: "Some heavier bursts [are expected] particularly across high ground in the north of England, where it will also be quite murky to start on Wednesday.

News.title: GCSE results 2026 times: When grades are released at schools and online on the Education Record app
News.content:
GCSE results 2026 times: When grades are released at schools and online on the Education Record app

GCSE results will be released online on the Education Records app for many students on Thursday

View Image (Image: PA)

Teenagers across the UK are set to find out their GCSE results on Thursday after sitting their exams earlier this summer. For the first time this year GCSE results will be available to many students online.

‌



Most students will typically collect results from school on Thursday morning, and timings may vary depending on the school. This year, students can access grades through the Education Record app, after a trial involving 95,000 pupils in Manchester and the West Midlands last summer.

‌



The app offers a digital record for future use when applying for further education or employment and will be updated on results day.

‌



What time are GCSE results released in schools?

GCSE results can be released to students by schools from 8am on Thursday, the exact time pupils receive their grades will depend on their school and what the teachers have decided.

Individual schools set their own collection arrangements and will inform students what time they should arrive on site to pick up their envelopes.

‌



Are GCSE results released online?

For the first time this year many GCSE students will be able to see their results online on the Education Record App. Results will update online on the Education Record app at 11am.

The Department of Education announced the £30m app in January. Schools using the app need to provide a QR code to pupils to link to their record.

What happens if you can't collect your GCSE results on Thursday?

Pupils who are away on holiday, unwell or otherwise unable to make it to their school or have access to the app can typically arrange in advance to receive their results by email or post.

Article continues below

Emails will generally arrive on results day, or grades sent via post may take longer to reach students.

Arrangements differ between schools. Students may also be able to nominate someone else to collect their results, although that person will typically need a signed letter and photo ID.

News.title: Schoolboy, 15, faces trial accused of 18 sex attacks including rape of girl aged 10
News.content:
Schoolboy, 15, faces trial accused of 18 sex attacks including rape of girl aged 10

All of the alleged offences are said to have happened between June 2023 and January 2025, when the defendant was aged between 12 and 14 years old

View Image The accused today appeared at Northampton Crown Court (Image: SWNS)

A 15-year-old schoolboy is set to stand trial accused of 18 sex attacks on eight different girls - including two counts of rape against two alleged victims, one of who is said to have been aged 10.

‌



The defendant, who cannot be named due to their age, is facing two counts of rape, 15 sex assaults and one assault by penetration towards his alleged victims, who were all aged between 10 and 15 at the time.

‌



The boy also faces four other counts, including two separate counts of making indecent photographs of a child, possession of a prohibited image of a child and possessing an extreme pornographic image. It is claimed all of the alleged offences took place between June 2023 and January 2025, when the defendant was aged between 12 and 14-years-old.

‌



He today appeared at Northampton Crown Court where he had been expected to give pleas to all 22 charges. However, Judge Adrienne Lucking KC began the hearing by ruling that he would not be asked to do so as she said he had not had enough time to consult with his new barrister.

The boy, who was wearing a black hoodie and black jeans, was not asked to enter the dock and instead took a seat at the back of the court where he was accompanied by his mother. In contrast to usual Crown Court etiquette, the judge referred to him by his first name throughout the 15-minute hearing and said he will be given an intermediary to help him understand what is happening during the next hearing and his proposed trial.

He spoke only to confirm his name, telling the judge "Yes, your honour". Throughout the hearing he stared straight ahead at the judge with his hands on top of each other, before later resting his chin on one hand.

‌



He is now due to give his pleas at the same court on September 25. The judge told him his mum will again be allowed to sit with him during that hearing. She also ruled that there will be pre-recorded cross examination of all the witnesses, which she added "will hopefully be done this year".

No details of the charges were said at today's hearing, but the court indictment listed all of his alleged offences, including the rape of a 10-year-old girl in April 2024. The defendant is also accused of rape against another girl in October 2024.

Moreover, he is accused of three sexual assaults against a third girl, who was aged 12 at the time, between June 2023 and September 2023. A fourth alleged victim has accused him of committing two sexual assaults against her between June 2024 and September 2024.

Article continues below

A fifth girl claims he committed two sexual assaults against her in October 2024. A sixth has accused him of committing three sexual assaults and assault by penetration against her between December 2024 and January 2025.

A seventh alleged victim claims he committed four sexual assaults against her, between December 2024 and January 2025. And an eighth girl has accused him of committing sexual assault against her between April 2024 and May 2024.

The boy previously appeared at Wellingborough Youth Court last month where a judge told him his alleged offences were too serious to be dealt with under their jurisdiction. He has been granted conditional bail instructing him not to contact the alleged victims, to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16, and to engage with the Northamptonshire Youth Justice Service.

News.title: Butlin's cancels bookings and offers refunds as adult attraction is closed
News.content:
Butlin's cancels bookings and offers refunds as adult attraction is closed

The attraction was an adults-only zone where grown ups could unwind. However, this has now been closed, with customers who've booked their spot in advance being contacted for a refund

View 2 Images Butlin's has closed the facility at its Bognor Regis site (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Butlin's has confirmed the closure of an attraction in its Bognor Regis park, with customers who had bookings saying they're "gutted" by the news.

The park was home to Ocean Spa, a part of the resort primarily aimed at the adult market, with 13- to 17-year-olds admitted only if accompanied by an over-18. The spa included a steam room, sauna, heated tiled loungers, a hydrospa, and a sun terrace, allowing for relaxing spa days and a variety of treatments.

The spa, the last of its kind in its parks, is now set to close on August 28. Butlin's is contacting customers with existing bookings to offer them their money back. Previously, the holiday park operator also operated a spa at its Skegness park, which closed in 2021.

View 2 Images The Ocean Spa will close at the end of the month (Image: Butlin's )

Josh Engleman, communications manager at Butlin's, said: "We can confirm we'll be closing our spa at Butlin’s Bognor Regis. We've contacted the small number of guests who had booked to visit the spa and they will, of course, receive a full refund.

"The spa has always been a small part of the resort experience. Our focus is on the activities and entertainment that families come to Butlin’s for, including recent additions such as PLAYXPERIENCE, which opened at Bognor Regis last year."

Butlin's customers have taken to social media to express their disappointment in the news. One posted a copy of the email she received confirming her cancellation, and commented: "We going in October and just got this. Gutted. First year my daughter is old enough."

Another said: "What a massive mistake! This was one of the only things for adults to relax and have a break from the kids! Such a disappointment." While another complained: "Why close the spa? We need a place to de-stress!", accompanied by a string of angry emojis.

While the spa closure has been confirmed, Butlin's has announced some new facilities in its parks in recent months. It recently added self-service bars to its parks, allowing people on both self-catering and all-inclusive packages to skip the queues and easily pour their own pints, soft drinks, and cocktails.

It also added bookable karaoke pods, where groups of up to 12 can choose from 45,000 chart-topping hits and throwback tunes, with a 55-minute session costing £36. You can even keep the party going by ordering drinks to your pod.

PLAYXPERIENCE was also added to Butlin's Bognor Regis in autumn 2024, a 50,000 square feet activity centre that offers nine experiences across two floors for kids and adults. These include escape rooms, a virtual reality arcade, laser tag, and hi-tech mini golf courses.

In addition to family holidays, Butlin's also continues to offer its adult-only Big Weekenders for visitors who'd prefer to enjoy the parks without kids around. These include themed weekends based around music genres and decades.

News.title: One dead and two injured in stabbing on London street as police swarm area
News.content:
One dead and two injured in stabbing on London street as police swarm area

Emergency services rushed to Askew Road in Shepherd’s Bush after reports of a stabbing on Tuesday morning.

View Image A person has died and two others injured after a stabbing in west London. (Image: MyLondon/Submitted)

A person has died and two others have been taken to hospital after a stabbing in west London.

‌



Emergency services were called to Askew Road in Shepherd’s Bush at 8.22am on Tuesday, with ambulance crews arriving at the scene in less than five minutes.

‌



Three people were treated by paramedics, with two taken to hospital and another pronounced dead at the scene, reports MyLondon. The conditions of those injured are not yet known.

‌



Officers and London’s Air Ambulance were also sent to the area, where a large cordon was put in place. A forensics tent was also later seen at the scene.

The Metropolitan Police has been contacted for further details, including whether any arrests have been made.

Article continues below

A spokesperson for London Ambulance Service said: “We were called at 8.22am today to reports of a stabbing on Askew Road, W12.

“We sent resources to the scene, including ambulance crews, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance. Our first crews arrived in less than five minutes.

“We treated three people in total. We took two patients to hospital but sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene.”

News.title: Lloyds, Halifax and Bank of Scotland outage recap: Thousands hit by app and online banking issues
News.content:
Lloyds, Halifax and Bank of Scotland customers were reporting online banking problems, with thousands of outage reports logged.

Lloyds, Halifax and Bank of Scotland outage recap: Thousands hit by app and online banking issues

Thousands of customers reported problems accessing Lloyds, Halifax and Bank of Scotland apps and online banking services on August 18.

Downdetector recorded around 2,450 reports for Lloyds, more than 1,000 for Halifax and over 340 for Bank of Scotland at the peak of the disruption.

All three banks acknowledged that some customers were experiencing problems and said they were working to restore services, before outage reports began to fall.

The issues have since been resolved, with customers now able to access app and online banking services as normal.

News.title: GCSE resits: How to retake exams, costs, dates, subjects and alternatives to maths and English
News.content:
GCSE resits: How to retake exams, costs, dates, subjects and alternatives to maths and English

View Image Schools, colleges and exam centres offer GCSE resit exams (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Students across the country are set to find out their GCSE results on Thursday after sitting exams earlier in the summer. Students whose grades are lower than what is required to move on to their next steps there is the option to resit tests.

‌



All students who are under the age of 18 who did not get at least a grade 4 will need to continue studying these subjects.

‌



Some sixth forms, colleges or apprenticeships might be flexible about entry requirements, especially if grades were only narrowly missed. Many colleges will allow students to retake GCSEs alongside studying for A level or T levels.

‌



Maths and English GCSE resits

Maths and English GCSE resit exams take place in November for both AQA and Pearson Edexcel, as well as the standard annual exam dates in May or June which take place each year.

Students on a 16 to 19 study programme and do not have a grade 4 or above in either English or maths will have to continue to study GCSE level English and maths. They will not be required to resit the exam as part of this.

‌



Some colleges and schools may offer a functional skills qualification in English or maths instead of a GCSE. This is a level 2 qualification based on learning how to apply English or maths in real life.

GCSE exam resits costs and prices

Many schools, colleges and sixth form centres will allow students to resit their exams for free in the following year from their first attempt, if the grade was below a 4. For those who passed with a Grade 4 or above, but still want to try to get a higher grade they are often charges associated with that.

Education centres usually charge between £75 to £150 per exam if they do charge. Private candidates could be charged between £150 to £500 by third party agencies and exam centres.

Article continues below

Where to resit GCSE exams

For students who have recently left school or are going to Sixth Form the best option is the former school or the sixth form centre they are planning to attend. Further Education colleges will offer some GCSE subjects, particularly English and maths. For those who are not in education there are private exam centres that accept external candidates for exams.

News.title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island
News.content:
A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said.

They have been named as newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert, who were in Greece on their honeymoon.

The private Bell 206 helicopter crashed just metres from a landing pad, killing the pair and their pilot, a Greek national.

The couple are said to have taken the helicopter from the village of Markopoulo near Athens to the popular holiday island, Kathimerini reported.

Greece's aviation safety authority told the BBC it was investigating the crash and that its investigators were heading to the scene on Tuesday to gather evidence and speak to witnesses.

News.title: PM says he's not embarrassed about hoax message exchange
News.content:
Andy Burnham says he is not embarrassed that he exchanged messages with a person posing as US President Donald Trump's chief of staff.

The prime minister added all politicians face "these challenges" but insisted he did "everything right" in how he handled the security breach.

News website Politico first reported, external that Burnham communicated with a person claiming to be Susie Wiles. Burnham said there was a "minimal exchange of information of zero consequence".

Liberal Democrat MP James MacCleary has written to Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee (ISC) to ask them to consider investigating what he called an "egregious security breach".

It is understood the communication between Burnham and the person posing as Wiles was in the form of messages and there was no conversation between the two.

Asked if he was embarrassed about the incident, Burnham told broadcasters: "No, I am not because there was a minimal exchange, nothing of consequence and quickly I realised that this needed to be reported and I did so.

"So I handled it in the right way. All politicians are receiving these pressures and these challenges, but I did everything right."

Pressed on what action is being taken to find out who was behind the incident and to improve systems, Burnham said the "correct action" had been taken both in the UK and the US, without providing further details.

MacCleary, in his letter to ISC chairman Lord Beamish, said the security of the prime minister's communications "ought to be an absolute priority".

He added: "We need to understand how this breach could occur, or else risk it being repeated."

News.title: How soon will the drought be over?
News.content:
It is the question many people are asking: when will the drought be over, and how much rain will it take for things to return to normal?

Contrary to public perception, a drought does not end with a few days of rain.

Water must flow back into rivers, reservoirs, and the stores beneath our feet in the tiny spaces between soil, sand, and rock. This can take months.

According to scientists, the key question is not "Has it rained?" but "have water resources recovered?"

News.title: Premier League chief says Fifa self-destructed over World Cup plan
News.content:
Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has criticised Fifa president Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan, saying the organisation has "pressed the self-destruct button" by delivering "a self-inflicted wound".

Infantino is under increasing pressure over his attempt, later abandoned, to create a new company to manage the commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% to be sold off to a private investment company.

Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) was aborted after widespread criticism from several confederations, led by Uefa, which has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

Masters backed the English Football Association's withdrawal of support for Infantino - and called for a new candidate for the presidency who could unify football.

"This is a problem of Fifa's making," Masters told BBC Sport.

"This is a self-inflicted wound. The organisation has pressed the self-destruct button, and the consequence of that flow now into the solutions to be that need to be found."

Masters was speaking in a wide-ranging interview before the start of the new Premier League season, which gets under way on Friday when champions Arsenal host promoted Coventry.

In it, Masters also said:

News.title: National Television Awards pick first all-female shortlist for drama acting award
News.content:
National Television Awards voters have selected an all-female shortlist in the best drama performance category for the first time.

The five nominees include previous winner Sheridan Smith, who played campaigner Ann Ming in ITV true crime drama I Fought The Law, and Gavin & Stacey's Ruth Jones for her role in Netflix thriller Run Away.

Vicky McClure gets the nod as Trigger Point's Lana Washington, while Ella Bruccoleri is shortlisted for alternative period drama The Other Bennet Sister, and Judy Parfitt is nominated for playing Sister Monica Joan in Call The Midwife.

The nominees were chosen in a public vote from an initial longlist that also included stars like David Tennant, Gary Oldman, Idris Elba, James Norton and Tom Hiddleston.

A second stage of voting is now open to pick the winners in the NTAs' 15 categories.

Elsewhere on this year's shortlists, Stacey Solomon has scored a hat-trick of nominations including best TV presenter.

That particular award was won last year by then-outgoing Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker, breaking Ant and Dec's remarkable 23-year winning run.

Solomon will go up against the Geordie duo for this year's gong as well as Sir David Attenborough in his 100th birthday year, Traitors and chat show host Claudia Winkleman and Alison Hammond.

In the inaugural celebrity-led reality docuseries award, Solomon and her partner Joe Swash face competition from boxer Tyson Fury, Jeremy Clarkson and Emmerdale actor-turned-farmer Kelvin Fletcher, as well as funny fishermen Bob Mortimer and Paul Whitehouse.

Mrs Brown's Boys â which this week officially cancelled its festive specials due to creator and star Brendan O'Carroll's broken jaw - has a nomination for best comedy.

Other nominated shows include Canadian breakout romance Heated Rivalry (for best new drama) - eligible as it was co-produced by Sky - and Winkleman and Tess Daly's final series of Strictly Come Dancing (for best talent show).

The NTAs, which recognise the best in British TV over the past twelve months, first launched in 1995 and the winners will be voted for by the public between now and midday on 8 September - the day of the ceremony.

Hosted again by comedian Joel Dommett, the event will take place at London's O2 arena and will be broadcast live on ITV1 and ITVX from 20:00 BST.

News.title: Earl Spencer to 'tell the truth' about his sister Princess Diana in new book
News.content:
Earl Spencer is to publish a new book telling the life story of his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales, from his perspective.

Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK next month, nearly 30 years after she died.

"I want to speak on Diana's behalf and do so in an openly positive way," Earl Spencer said of his reasons for writing the book.

He added that he hoped it would enable people to understand who she really was: "A one-off, dynamic character, full of love, charisma and self-doubt, who gave life a hell of a go, and left the world a far better place, despite exiting the stage while still so young."

Princess Diana, who died aged 36 following a car crash in Paris in 1997, would have turned 65 on 1 July this year.

Her sons Prince William and Prince Harry were aged 15 and 12 respectively at the time of her death.

In a statement released on Tuesday to mark the new book, Earl Spencer said he had been "inundated yet again" with requests for interviews about his sister, with the 30th anniversary of her death approaching.

"This has convinced me to write down my own thoughts and memories, once and for all, rather than having the discomfort of again reading the opinions of others, many of which are based on untruths that have become accepted over time," he said.

"The aim of this book is to tell the truth about Diana from her brother's perspective, just as I attempted to do when speaking at her funeral," he added, referring to the eulogy he delivered in Westminster Abbey in September 1997.

He said he hoped the book would be of interest to those who "still cherish" Diana's memory from when she was alive.

"And I would be delighted if those too young to remember her in her heyday feel - after reading this - that they 'get' who she really was," he continued.

News.title: Prevent not helping children fixated with violence, children's commissioner says
News.content:
The government's counter-extremism programme is not able to deal with the growing number of children being referred to it who are "fixated on violence without a clear ideology", the children's commissioner has said.

Referrals of children to Prevent have risen over the past decade - from 2,918 in 2016-17 to 4,715 in 2024-25 - and Dame Rachel de Souza said most were being sent back to schools without further action.

Dame Rachel said most children being referred did not identify with traditional forms of extremism and "stronger safeguarding" was needed for this group.

The government said it was reviewing the report and developing further options to "manage those fascinated with extreme violence".

Dame Rachel's report comes just over two years after three girls were killed while attending a dance class in Southport in July 2024.

Their attacker Axel Rudakubana was 17 at the time and had himself been referred to Prevent three times between 2019 and 2021 due to his interest in terrorist attacks and school shootings, but his case too had been closed because he did not have a clear ideology.

Prevent was set up 20 years ago to try to identify future potential terrorists and intervene in their lives, often by challenging hateful ideologies such as far right extremism or support for jihadist violence.

The second phase of the Southport Inquiry is examining how to deal with individuals who pose a risk of extreme violence but where ideology is not the primary driver, as well as the role of the internet and social media in influencing and enabling them.

A Prevent referral is one made to the police when there are concerns that a person may be susceptible to radicalisation or could be at risk of becoming involved in or supporting terrorism. Typically, for children, this process starts with potential concerning behaviour spotted by teachers or social workers.

Most child referrals are made by the education sector including schools - 60% in the year from April 2024 to March 2025.

The report by the children's commissioner found that most of these referrals were being sent back to the education sector because Prevent was not able to effectively deal with their cases - because its focus was on the risk of terrorism which generally means violence being carried out for an ideological objective.

Some 71% of child referrals were found to have "no specific extremist ideology identified".

Dame Rachel told the BBC many cases were linked to children being involved in the "most awful online communities, watching other children self-harm and trying to make them do that, obsessed with killers and school shootings" - material she said was illegal under the Online Safety Act.

"Counter-terrorism police and Prevent are excellent at deprogramming children who have been caught into ideological movements," she told BBC Radio 4's World at One programme.

"What they can't deal with is this, so we have to make sure there is a far wider response."

News.title: One dead and hundreds ill in UK salmonella outbreak
News.content:
Symptoms include stomach cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting or fever. These usually develop between 12 and 72 hours after becoming infected.

Anyone who is concerned should contact their GP or out of hours service in the first instance, says the UKHSA.

Most cases - 199 of the 207 - have been in England, including 47 in London and 38 in Yorkshire and Humber.

There have been six cases in Scotland, one in Wales and another in Northern Ireland.

Hannah Charles, lead epidemiologist for gastrointestinal infections at UKHSA, said: "We're working with Food Standards Agency and other public health agencies to investigate a salmonella outbreak that may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK."

Salmonella can be found in a number of food sources including raw or under-cooked poultry or meat and eggs.

Preparing and cooking food thoroughly can prevent infection, as well as washing your hands after using the bathroom and before handling food.

Thousands of cases food poisoning happen each year in the UK caused by lots of different strains of salmonella.

It is more unusual to see an outbreak like this linked to one specific strain of the bacterium affecting many people at one time.

Experts say it is likely there could be more cases to come and some people may have been unwell but not reported it.

The UKHSA says "extensive" epidemiological and food chain investigations are ongoing to identify the source but that egg consumption remains the strongest to date.

People appear to have fallen ill after eating out rather than after consuming food prepared at home.

Some of the food businesses linked to 24 of the cases use imported eggs.

"At this time there is no identified link to UK-produced eggs or poultry," says the UKHSA.

Any extra precautions or preventative measures will be implemented if needed, it says. The risk to the general public is low.

Jacquelyn McCormick, Head of Incidents at the Food Standards Agency, said eggs which are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.

She advised: "Infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only eat runny or raw eggs if they have a British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain egg assurance scheme."

People handling eggs, eggshells or egg packaging should wash their hands thoroughly with soap and water, she added.

News.title: Snooker player Graeme Dott goes on trial over child abuse allegations
News.content:
A former world snooker champion has gone on trial at the High Court in Glasgow over child sex abuse charges.

Graeme Dott, 49, is accused of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards two youngsters, a girl and a boy, between 1993 and 2010.

The alleged incidents are said to have occurred on "various occasions" and involved addresses in Glasgow's east end and South Lanarkshire as well as in a car.

Dott, who won the world title in 2006, has denied the charges against him.

The allegation involving a girl includes claims he inappropriately touched her, instructed her to remove her clothes and exposed himself.

In the claims surrounding the separate abuse of a boy, Dott is said to have made sexual remarks, entered a bathroom and watched him shower and also molested him.

The female witness, who is now in her 40s, claimed the first incident occurred when she was nine or 10 at a house in Glasgow.

She had initially been in a room with other youngsters when Dott came in.

News.title: Wetherspoons bans customers playing music from phones in pubs
News.content:
Wetherspoons has banned its customers from playing music out loud or taking calls on speaker, saying the noise from phones and tablets was an increasing problem driving people "nuts".

The company â which runs 792 pubs and bars across the UK â said that following complaints it has asked customers to switch their devices to silent or to use earphones.

Polling in recent years by various organisations suggests people are largely opposed to others playing music or taking calls on speaker in public spaces.

Wetherspoons told the BBC that staff would be asked to use "common sense" when enforcing the ban.

"We are not looking to ask anyone to leave a pub if they go against the ruling, but it is an option for managers if they refuse to do so," the company said.

The British Beer and Pub Association, which represents Wetherspoons and several other pub companies in the UK, said that "having a clear policy helps staff enforce rules and customers know what they can and can't do".

The group added: "We're yet to hear of anyone who relishes having a pint against the backdrop of a speakerphone call or someone loudly playing a video, so we expect this move will be greatly welcomed."

News.title: Actress Phyllida Law, mother of Emma and Sophie Thompson, dies at 94
News.content:
Born in Glasgow in 1932, Law attended the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, initially to become a stage designer but ended up studying acting instead "by happy accident".

She married fellow actor Eric Thompson - best known for The Magic Roundabout - in 1957.

The couple were together until he died of a heart attack aged 53, in 1982.

Throughout a career spanning eight decades, Law would go on to appear in numerous TV shows including Dickson of Dock Green and Rumpole of the Bailey before Midsomer Murders, Foyle's War, Doc Martin and New Tricks.

She was also known for her work on the big screen in films such as Anna Karenina, Saving Grace and Miss Potter.

On stage, Law appeared alongside Alec Guinness in John Mortimer's A Voyage Round My Father in London's West End in 1971, and in Alan Bennett's Habeas Corpus at the Oxford Playhouse in 1973, which then transferred to the capital.

She also played Jacqueline in the original London cast of La Cage Aux Folles at the London Palladium in 1986.

The actress starred alongside John Hurt in a short film entitled Love at First Sight which was shortlisted for an Oscar in 2012.

Law received an OBE in 2014 for services to drama and for charitable services.

Her daughters have both gone on to enjoy success on screen.

Emma was born in 1959 and has won two Oscars - one for acting in Howard's End and another for writing the screenplay for Sense and Sensibility - and is also known for featuring in Love Actually and the Harry Potter film series.

Sophie was born in 1964 and has appeared in films including Gosford Park and Four Weddings and a Funeral, and been nominated for seven Olivier Awards on stage.

Speaking about her daughters to the Telegraph in 2017, external, Law said: "They are both my colleagues in a way. They didn't follow in our footsteps, they rushed past us, trampling on us."

The family acting dynasty has continued with Dame Emma's daughter Gaia, who posted on Instagram about her grandmother: "Rest well my queen."

Speaking of her love of the arts to the Telegraph, Law joked: "I've got to have my funeral in the afternoon, curtain up 2.30pm, so people can get to the theatre afterwards."

News.title: Serco employee charged over sharing asylum seeker addresses
News.content:
An employee of a company that provides accommodation for asylum seekers has been charged with misconduct in public office over sharing the properties' addresses.

Houses in St John's Way, Bracken Road, Clover Way, Elm Road and Chester Way in Thetford, Norfolk, were targeted by crowds over three nights earlier this month.

James Jobson, 62, from Highlow Road, Costessey, near Norwich, works at Serco and appeared at Ipswich Magistrates' Court on Monday.

He was remanded in custody and will appear at Norwich Crown Court on 14 September.

The charge stated that between 3 and 14 August, while acting as a public officer employed by Serco, Jobson "wilfully and without reasonable excuse or justification" committed misconduct in a way which "amounted to an abuse of the public's trust in the office".

Norfolk Police said the charge was in connection to the "release of information relating to a number of addresses in Thetford, which were later targeted during several nights of violent disorder in the town".

A spokesperson for Serco said: "This matter is currently being handled by the police, and we are cooperating fully. As this relates to an ongoing legal process, it would be inappropriate to comment further."

News.title: Ferguson shipyard to cut a quarter of its workforce
News.content:
Scotland's state-owned shipyard is to cut nearly a quarter of its total workforce while it waits for confirmation of promised new orders.

Workers at Ferguson Marine have been invited to apply for voluntary redundancy as construction draws to a close on the second of two long-delayed CalMac ferries.

The Port Glasgow firm currently employs 247 core staff, 31 agency staff and 32 apprentices - but says it expects to shed 70 posts through a voluntary redundancy process.

The Scottish government has promised to directly award the yard new orders for four smaller ships, but ministers say they are still conducting "due diligence" on the plan.

Ferguson Marine said the job losses would protect the long-term viability of the yard - but unions described the move as "a betrayal of a blameless workforce".

BBC Scotland News understands those who choose to leave the firm will receive Â£1,000 per completed year of service, up to Â£10,000, on top of their statutory entitlements.

News.title: Disabled people in England to get 24-hour free bus travel
News.content:
Disabled people in England will be able to travel by bus for free at any time of day from April, the government has announced.

Currently, disabled bus passes are only eligible for use between the hours of 09:30 and 23:00 on weekdays, making it difficult for people to get to work or attend later evening events. They can be used at any time of day at the weekend and on bank holidays.

It is believed about one million people could benefit from the change, which forms part of the government's focus on reducing the cost of living and encouraging people into work.

The disability charity Scope said the move would "remove barriers to everyday life".

According to the government, bus travel is the most popular mode of transport in England and a "lifeline for so many".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it was "simply not right that many disabled people cannot travel using their pass during certain times of the day".

He said the government would change that, as he had done previously in his role as mayor of Greater Manchester.

Earlier this year, Burnham removed time-restricted travel for those with disabled passes in Manchester so they could use the city's bus system, known as the Bee Network, at any time of day.

"I'm proud to do it now for the whole country," he added.

Tom Gordon, Liberal Democrat MP for Harrogate and Knaresborough and prominent advocate for the policy, called it a "huge win for the disabled community" and a "culmination of two years of campaigning".

But a Conservative Party spokesman asked the prime minister to "come clean" on how he was going to fund "this growing list of policies".

"This is simply the shuffling around of existing departmental budgets," they added.

News.title: Ex-workers tell of 'chaotic atmosphere' at new £400m prison
News.content:
The UK's newest prison has had a "chaotic atmosphere" in its first 18 months, former workers have told a BBC investigation.

HMP Millsike, in East Yorkshire, was heralded by the government for setting "the standard for the future" when it opened in March 2025 with 1,500 places.

But former workers have described under-staffing, inadequate training and seeing specialist officers called in to deal with serious incidents on numerous occasions.

Mitie, the company that runs the category C prison, said safety was its "highest priority" and it was "operating in line with plans agreed with the Ministry of Justice".

News.title: Watch: Seven GCSE exams, five months, one determined teenager
News.content:
Secondary school pupil Patrick McCabe, 16, has told BBC Breakfast that the wait for his GCSE results on Thursday is "terrifying".

McCabe has cerebral palsy and completed exams in seven subjects over the course of five months using eye-gaze technology - an achievement celebrated by his friends and teachers at school.

The pupil, who describes himself as "hard-working, resilient and a little bit cheeky," said the process was difficult.

McCabe was inspired to take the exams after seeing the late Rob Burrow appear on CBeebies' Bedtime Stories, where he read aloud using an eye-controlled computer.

BBC Breakfast's Jayne McCubbin spoke to Patrick ahead of results day.

Christmas is coming early for State Farm auto insurance customers.

The nation’s largest auto insurer recently announced $5 billion in dividend payments for customers - the largest in company history. Drivers will receive 4 percent -10 percent of premiums they paid in 2025.

“That translated this year to lower auto rates and cash back in the form of a $5 billion policyholder dividend,” CEO Jon Farney said.

Drivers of more than 49 million vehicles are slated for payments. Several million have already received their money, the company said, and remaining dividends will be sent out in the next few months.

State Farm is notifying drivers eligible for a share of the $5 billion payout by email or letter.

open image in gallery After three straight years of auto insurance premium increases, drivers paid less, on average, for their car policies in 2025, leading State Farm and a big competitor to issue dividends ( Getty )

Customers who had State Farm policies in 2025 but no longer do so still may be eligible for payouts, the company said. State Farm is a mutual insurance company, which means policyholders have the chance to share in the company’s yearly profits through dividends.

This year’s dividend is the first such payout for auto insurance customers since 2021, when 2020 policyholders received $1.9 billion, according to State Farm records.

Mutual insurance competitor USAA issued at least $3.8 billion in dividends for 2025 - the largest in its company history.

The record-breaking payouts are due to, in part, a combination of fewer claims and changing rates, according to an August analysis by insurance marketplace Insurify. Average auto insurance rates hit record highs in 2024 after three consecutive years of annual increases.

open image in gallery Auto insurance claims were down in 2025, leading to better margins for auto insurers and dividends for State Farm customers ( AFP/Getty )

“Those high premiums helped car insurance companies recover financially and enter 2025 in a more stable position,” Insurify said.

Some 39 states saw their average auto insurance rates fall in 2025. The consumer-friendly rate environment may come to an end in 2026, though. Insurify predicted rates will rise around 1 percent in 2026, with 32 states “on track” to have higher average rates this year.

Some 11 states have seen auto insurance premiums fall in 2026, August data from insurance marketplace The Zebra notes. Most states’ insurance rates experienced minor increases of under $100.

Louisiana has the highest rates in the nation, while Vermont, Wyoming and North Carolina have the lowest rates, The Zebra found.

“There have been lots of state-by-state decreases for carriers this year,” The Zebra CCO David Seider said. “I expect to see some states have meaningful premium drops on a per-carrier basis.

Donald Trump’s top federal prosecutor in Washington, D.C. has twice failed to keep an alleged World War II memorial vandal in jail after government lawyers demanded that she stay behind bars while awaiting trial on two felony charges.

A federal judge rejected U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro’s second attempt to keep Melissa Farris in jail on Tuesday morning after he ordered her released one day earlier.

Pirro, whose job could be on the line after she delivered a stunning rebuke of the Trump administration’s attempts to prosecute a former Olympian over damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, has gone to unusual lengths to keep Farris in jail for the alleged vandalism, which her office called a “brazen attack on one of the Nation’s most sacred monuments.”

Farris, according to Pirro, poses an “exceptionally high risk of flight” — which a federal judge flatly denied.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh ordered her release on Monday, and he swiftly denied Pirro’s second attempt on Tuesday morning, stating that Pirro’s office “essentially just recycles the same arguments” that he rejected one day earlier.

open image in gallery US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who has failed to keep another alleged vandal in jail, is reportedly on thin ice with President Donald Trump after dropping charges against a former Olympian accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ( Getty )

Sharbaugh ordered Farris to remain outside D.C. and report to federal pretrial officials in Ohio pending trial. He did not impose electronic monitoring or require a third-party custodian, which prosecutors later requested.

According to a complaint filed last week, prosecutors claimed Farris, 41, had spray-painted “Clean Hands Dirty $” on the memorial and splattered paint on its stonework. She also is accused of pouring detergent into a fountain that filled it with foam and bubbles.

Farris livestreamed the incident and posted videos on social media appearing to acknowledge the vandalism.

She later turned herself into police in Virginia.

“If anyone is a flight risk, it is certainly her,” Pirro said in a statement.

The National Park Service estimated that clearing up the damage cost more than $1,000, according to prosecutors.

open image in gallery Melissa Farris, 41, faces two felony charges for allegedly vandalizing the World War 2 Memorial in Washington DC ( VIDEO BY MELISSA LOVEWELL/SCREENSHOT RELEASED BY US ATTORNEY PIRRO VIA X/via REUTERS )

Pirro’s latest failure follows the implosion of several high-profile cases surrounding Trump’s controversial renovations of the nation’s capital and his federal takeover, including failed prosecutions of D.C. protesters and people accused of vandalizing newly renovated projects.

Grand juries have repeatedly declined to indict people at the center of politically loaded cases, and juries at trial have also rejected the government’s efforts to prosecute protesters caught up in the administration’s military occupation of the capital.

Weeks after she publicly accused 67-year-old Olympian David Heard of “forcefully and violently” ripping out the Reflecting Pool’s Trump-requested blue liner, Pirro filed a stunning motion to dismiss the case entirely — outraging Trump, who has spent weeks demanding prosecutors target alleged vandals despite his administration appearing to admit that the damage was caused by contractors.

In a court filing asking for charges to be dropped, Pirro’s office admitted that the sealant started to peel “almost immediately” after the work was completed. It was not until after the indictment was filed that Trump’s Department of Interior determined that the “damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism,” according to Pirro.

“She folded like an umbrella,” Trump said from the Oval Office earlier this month. “I think she choked.”

The judge overseeing that case agreed to dismiss charges against Hearn and will hold a hearing next month on whether the dismissal should be granted “with prejudice,” which would prevent the Justice Department from charging him for the same alleged conduct.

With her job apparently on the line over her repeated failure to deliver on cases that Trump wants to prosecute, Pirro is reportedly launching a special grand jury that critics fear could be weaponized to deliver spurious investigations into the president’s political enemies.

Emergency responders are attending an incident off the Sussex coast following reports of four people in difficulty in the open water.

Several ambulances and two air ambulances were seen near the RNLI station in Shoreham-by-Sea, West Sussex, on Tuesday afternoon.

A Sussex Police spokesperson said: “Emergency services are currently responding to reports of four people in difficulty in the water close to Shoreham Fort.

“A section of the A259 in Shoreham has been closed as the incident remains ongoing, and we’re urging the public to stay clear of the area in the meantime

“We will provide more information as soon as we are able to.”

The A259 Brighton Road was blocked in both directions from New Road to Kingston Lane because of the incident.

An RNLI spokesman said: “Shoreham RNLI were tasked by HM Coastguard at approximately 3pm on Tuesday 18 August.”

At the scene an ambulance could be seen leaving under a police escort with blue lights flashing.

A HM Coastguard spokesman added: “HM Coastguard responded to an incident reported at Shoreham at about 2.45pm on 18 August.

“An HM Coastguard helicopter was sent as well as Littlehampton, Shoreham and Newhaven Coastguard Rescue Teams, and an RNLI lifeboat from Shoreham.

“Sussex Police and South East Coast Ambulance Service also attended.”

The South East Coast Ambulance Service also said they were responding to reports that four people needed medical attention after getting into difficulty in the water near Shoreham Harbour.

“We were called shortly after 3pm and have a number of ambulance resources at the scene,” a spokeswoman said.

“We have no further information to share at this time but will provide updates as soon as possible.”
