Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 14: Liverpool
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 4th (NB: this is not necessarily Andy Hunter’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 5th

Prospects

Andoni Iraola did not have to be sold on Liverpool when they came calling for a coach courted also by Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace after his sterling work at Bournemouth. This is just as well as the sales pitch did not come with bells and whistles attached. “When I came here, the owners told me everything is not perfect,” the new head coach revealed at his unveiling. “They said we would have some challenges, we would have to replace important players leaving, we have some injuries, but we are here to solve these kind of problems.” Validating last summer’s expensive recruitment strategy, restoring the faith of the Anfield crowd and rebuilding in an impatient environment can be added to that list.

Liverpool were enticed by Iraola’s style of play, but his ability to step back and problem-solve – taking Bournemouth into Europe last season despite losing most of his defence in the summer and Antoine Semenyo in January, for example – will have also appealed. Arne Slot was assailed by unprecedented challenges last season, including the death of Diogo Jota and Mohamed Salah’s attempts to undermine his manager in public, and lost his way as a result. How much of last season’s regression can be pinned on the former head coach will become apparent in the months ahead.

Similarly to Slot in 2024, Iraola has been bequeathed a rich inheritance in terms of individual talent. Unlike his predecessor, however, he is starting from a lower base in terms of constructing a team. With Salah gone and no replacement installed, as yet, responsibility has increased on Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to produce after their underwhelming debut seasons. Wirtz has been deployed just behind Isak in pre-season and the early signs have been promising. Central midfield options are strong and Dominik Szoboszlai’s new five-year contract removes one distraction. Questions remain over Liverpool’s threat from out wide, their defensive resources and leadership within the team, but having worked towards this moment throughout his coaching career Iraola will be confident of finding answers.

Off-field picture

In contrast to last summer there has been more upheaval behind the scenes with a change of head coach, Michael Edwards departing as chief executive of football for the owners, Fenway Sports Group, and the sporting director, Richard Hughes, expected to follow suit once the transfer window closes. But one issue dominates: the arrival of the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin and Amit Bhatia, son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, as part of a consortium that has bought 30% of Liverpool for £1.65bn. That several of the world’s richest people have bought into Liverpool underlines the attractiveness of the club, commercially and otherwise, but beyond Bhatia becoming vice-chairman on an expanded board it remains to be seen what the deal truly means for the club and its fans.

Owner-fan relationship

FSG’s habit of annoying and then appeasing the Liverpool fanbase returned last season when it abandoned plans to lock in ticket prices rises over a three-year period. The owners were thanked for engaging with supporters, after widespread protests , but there are now weightier conversations to be had in light of their deal with the 1892 Holdings consortium. As the supporters union, Spirit of Shankly, asked in an open letter: “Is this part of a planned wider sale, or a one-off? What due diligence is being done on the potential investors/owners? This is about their plans, reasons for purchase and involvement in sports or business elsewhere.” FSG insist the deal is not an exit strategy from a club they purchased for £300m in 2010 but will increase global business, technology and investment opportunities.

The manager

After sacking Slot it was no surprise Liverpool turned to a coach who promises the kind of aggressive, front-foot style Anfield openly pined for last season. Iraola, who was lured from Rayo Vallecano by Hughes when the Liverpool sporting director worked for Bournemouth, was the only candidate Liverpool spoke to in their quick transition from the Slot era. The 44-year-old Basque has no silverware, or even European experience on his CV, but his record of consistently improving attractive teams, which resulted in Bournemouth qualifying for Europe for the first time in their history last season, made him one of the most coveted coaches available this summer.

Stat attack

Liverpool had a weird, erratic campaign in 2025-26. Only Aston Villa and Manchester City had a longer run of Premier League wins yet only four teams (including Chelsea and Tottenham) had a worse losing streak. Their four-draw stretch in January was only topped by Bournemouth and Brentford. Iraola was unbeaten in his final 18 league matches last season and will need to bring similar consistency to Liverpool.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Jeremy Jacquet celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the pre-season friendly against Como. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Liverpool would love the answer to be Bradley Barcola (and for Paris Saint-Germain to lower their asking price for the France international) but as that pursuit continues it is another arrival from Ligue 1 who could prove their most important recruit so far, Jérémy Jacquet. A £55m deal rising to £60m was completed with Rennes in February, just days before the 21-year-old sustained a shoulder injury that ended his season, after Liverpool had been in the market for a young central defender with vast potential for some time. Jacquet’s recovery has affected his first pre-season at Anfield, but he is considered an immediate, if inexperienced, solution to a problem position and impressed on his first outing against Como.

Set for a breakthrough

There may be more opportunities for Rio Ngumoha depending on how Liverpool’s winger chase goes, but, of all the young talents on display this summer, no one pushed their claims further than Trey Nyoni. Nyoni and Ngumoha were part of Slot’s stretched first team squad last season, but the former’s involvement was limited to six substitute appearances in the Premier League plus eight cup outings. The 19-year-old looked immediately at ease in pre-season with Iraola’s instructions for quick, forward passes from his central midfielders and embraced responsibility. Nyoni faces fierce competition to establish himself, but appears ready to make the step up.

World Cup impact

The first pre-season is hugely important to a new coach, but post-World Cup holidays deprived Iraola of eight players when Liverpool reported back. He will have had a full squad together for three weeks by the time the season starts at Newcastle, injuries excluded. The tournament brought deflating exits for several Liverpool players, including Virgil van Dijk, Alisson and Florian Wirtz, but also a welcome reminder of Alexis Mac Allister’s talents as the midfielder helped Argentina reach a second successive final. Mac Allister was not alone in struggling last season, but showed this summer just how influential he can be.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Infantino wields the axe after Lamour breaks rank inside Fifa’s fiefdom
Sports.content:
SO BE IT

A senior Fifa blazer held in such rare high regard that the prescient synth-pop duo Erasure named a single after him long before he entered the intoxicating world of football administration, Kevin Lamour was a lone dissenting voice inside Fifa’s lair when Gianni Infantino’s plot to flog part of the World Cup to private investors – potentially on the cheap – was rumbled last month. A plan so half-baked it succeeded only in ruining the holidays of Proper Journalists who naively hoped they might enjoy some leisure time after weeks of being studiously ignored by Gianni in the foyers of various luxury hotels dotted across North America, the then chief operating officer of Fifa had witheringly described the sell-off proposal as “the project of one person”. Refusing to sign off on the deal, Lamour said the administration had been “deceived” by Gianni, adding that if speaking up against his boss “means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

While Football Daily presumes the Frenchman has been dozing with one eye open during the fortnight or so that has passed since he aired his reservations in what will have been viewed as an act of gross insubordination, it is worth noting that Gianni’s wheeze was quietly shelved just a few days afterwards. On Monday night, however, Lamour will have slept the sleep of the just after being handed his P45 and booted through the door marked ‘Do One!’ by his now former paymasters. “Fifa can confirm that the working relationship between Fifa and Kevin Lamour as Fifa’s Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026,” honked a spokesperson. “Fifa thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future. No further comment will be made on the matter.”

Given their now customary lack of transparency, it is no surprise that Fifa is not planning on commenting any further on the matter, but others have been eager to have their say. Never backwards in coming forwards and a constant thorn in Gianni’s side, it was no surprise to see Lise Klavness, head of the Norwegian Football Association shouting from the first cab off the rank. “Now he is thrown out and we are supposed to move on,” she fumed. “It’s unacceptable, it’s management by fear,” she said of the treatment meted out to Lamour, a man she described as the best football administrator she has ever met. “Now we also have to call upon Fifa leadership and the administration to not submit to orders you know are not in the interests of football.”

While the evidence of the Geopolitics World Cup and its aftermath suggest Klaveness might have more luck calling upon fish to stop swimming, her comments have been interpreted as a dig at the Swedish Fifa blazer Mattias Grafström, who is understood to have sacked Lamour at the behest of Gianni, who continues to cling on to power like a barnacle on a ship’s hull. “Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go,” wrote Grafström in an email sent to staff. “The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue.” For now, it seems the Fifa sackings will continue until morale improves.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Guys I want to confess something, I’m [eff]ing divorced from the most beautiful woman on your planet. It’s my wife, my ex-wife – I love her unbelievably, but we lost the passion. For many reasons, we lost the passion. I love her? Yes, absolutely. She loves me? Yes, but we lost the passion. How do you play football, because you are paid? Or because of something inside? Where is the passion? In your life, whatever you are going to do, do it with passion. I don’t want any good players. I want players with passion” – in a new Amazon documentary, Pep Guardiola is shown using revelations about his private life to try to end a poor run of results. Yep. Another relationship issue is exposed when the former City manager has a big barney with Kyle Walker.

View image in fullscreen Pep Guardiola, doing his thing. Photograph: Tom Flathers/Amazon

double quotation mark Upon reading the final article in Monday’s missive [full email edition – Football Daily Ed], I noted the final sentence of Memory Lane commenced with “(insert name of whoever is in the news as being on the end of a bad foul, bad behaviour, etc, here)”. I may be doing you a gross disservice but I couldn’t help feeling this was a Wizard of Oz moment where the curtain was momentarily drawn back, revealing (insert witty denouement here)” – Anthony Brady.

double quotation mark Further to Monday’s letter about players’ wages. To put things into perspective, if we estimate the average Premier League player’s wage to be, say, £5m per annum, or £100,000 per week, this works out that in one week such a player gets (hardly earns) more than the likes of Jimmy Greaves earned in his complete football career. If we go back to players like Finney, Milburn and Lofthouse the difference is even greater” – Stewart McGuinness.

double quotation mark I’m glad Rob Smyth was dissing a lousy movie and not the Gigli, Beniamino, the Italian tenor, in my humble opinion the best there ever has been. Well, I needed something to take my mind off the football!” – Bob Cushion.

Sports.title: Patrick Vieira appointed as head coach of Senegal, the country of his birth
Sports.content:
Patrick Vieira has been appointed as the head coach of Senegal. The Senegal-born former Arsenal captain has been out of work since leaving his post as manager of the Serie A side Genoa last November and replaces Pape Thiaw, who was dismissed after Senegal’s defeat by Belgium in the last 32 at this summer’s World Cup.

“Mr Patrick Vieira is the new coach of the Senegalese national A team,” read a statement. “The date of the official presentation and the next steps in its installation will be communicated at a later date. Welcome to Senegal, coach.”

Vieira won three Premier League titles with Arsenal, as well as the World Cup and European Championship with France in 1998 and 2000 respectively. After managerial spells with Nice and New York City, the 50-year-old spent two years in charge of Crystal Palace.

He was sacked by the south London club in March 2023 and joined Strasbourg as head coach before a 12-month stint in Italy.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Dedic completes £29.5m Newcastle move, Vicario joins Juventus
Sports.content:
The chance to be reunited with Matthias Jaissle convinced Amar Dedic to swap Benfica for Newcastle in a £29.5m transfer. Dedic becomes Newcastle’s sixth signing of a turbulent summer on Tyneside and the 24-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international is likely to start at right-back at home to Liverpool on Sunday.

“Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me,” said Dedic, who previously played for Newcastle’s new manager at RB Salzburg. “We know each other well; he knows what I can bring to the pitch and I’m really happy to play for him again. It’s a special feeling and a real honour to join Newcastle.”

With Tino Livramento still recovering from a calf injury, Newcastle’s lack of senior right-backs has been highlighted in pre-season and, soon after replacing Eddie Howe earlier this month, Jaissle advised club executives that Dedic could fill the void. It helps that a defender also comfortable at left-back understands the German’s playing philosophy.

Juventus confirmed they have signed goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario ⁠from Tottenham on a season-long loan. The ⁠deal includes an option for Juve to make the ⁠move permanent at the end of ​the season, ‌Tottenham said.

Vicario, ‌29, joined Spurs from Empoli ‌in 2023 and made 117 appearances for the north London club. He was part of the side ‌that won the Europa League in 2025, ending the ​club’s 17-year wait for a major trophy, but lost his place to Antonin Kinsky following the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi as manager in March.

Sunderland, meanwhile, are set to announce the acquisition of a new left-back on Tuesday after fending off competition from Roma and Newcastle to sign the 20-year-old Toulouse defender Dayann Methalie for £25.6m.

The France Under-21 international made 28 Ligue 1 appearances last season and will compete with Reinildo for a place in Régis Le Bris’ team. Methalie, who has signed a five-year contract at the Stadium of Light, is also comfortable operating as a left-sided central defender or at wing-back.

Sports.title: Interviewing José Mourinho: ego, charisma, talent and his ‘rucksack of pain’
Sports.content:
Even in the hyperreal world of football, there are few characters more compelling, more polarising, or more everything than José Mourinho, the best and worst of public him on full display in a new three-part Netflix series. “It reminded me how good he was,” says Joe Pearlman, who directed Mourinho, and the actual Mourinho is, believe it or not, keen to communicate the same. As he puts it in the show: “I look, you look, I see more than you.”

Making documentaries, though, is often about taking people to the places they’re most skilled at avoiding. “I knew the interviews were going to be very intense,” says Pearlman, “and he was going to try and control the narrative and manipulate us. Everything bad is everyone else’s fault and everything he’s done is validated by winning. Because that’s all that’s important.”

This is just one aspect of an unusual worldview. “There’s a moment in episode three where I ask him about his childhood,” says Pearlman, “and he doesn’t want to talk about it because he doesn’t think it’s relevant to who he is, essentially saying he’s not interested in people. Which, for one of the greatest man-managers of all time, is quite odd.”

The son of a much-loved coach, Mourinho felt like an outsider from childhood because he was known by way of his dad. Then, when he became a coach himself, having not been a player, that appeared to confer insider privilege. Indisputably, this self-image has helped Mourinho self-actualise, surviving unlimited wealth at Chelsea and a spell at Real Madrid, with the attitude of “someone who’s had a chip on their shoulder for a lot of their life” – along, of course, with his irrepressible charisma and tactical acumen.

Félix Mourinho died in June 2017 and, when that comes up in the documentary, there are tears. “He’s obviously buried the loss of his father,” Pearlman says. “It’s very painful for him to talk about. As someone who’s lost a parent, I can talk about my mum very openly because I’ve processed it. I’ve been to therapy, I’ve tried to understand what that part of my life means. I don’t think José’s ever tried to understand what any part of his life means. I think he’s always looking forward, always looking for the next thing. He’s winning the treble for Inter against Louis van Gaal and Bayern but, at the same time, he’s really thinking about crushing Pep [Guardiola] when he joins Madrid.

“Losing his father changed him; it tainted the years that came afterwards. And on top of that, José carries every word, every goal, every decision that doesn’t go his way; it’s a rucksack of pain he’s been lugging around since he was probably 19, 20 years old.”

Nevertheless, everything that makes Mourinho special – the wit, the insight, the confidence, the zest, the charm, the genius, the cool – burns through the screen. “He was looking for an outlet to be the biggest possible version of himself and football allowed that,” says Pearlman. “The ego and the charisma on top of the talent meant he could embody a character he’d always dreamt of being, that maybe he wasn’t in his childhood, and that is the person that we’ve come to know as José Mourinho.”

View image in fullscreen ‘I don’t think José’s ever tried to understand what any part of his life means,’ says Pearlman. Photograph: Netflix

That person is, of course, only one version of reality, a character honed for the purpose of footballing warfare. One who, it seems, sees football as distinct from the real world, with combatants permitted to do anything in the pursuit of victory; he is no more apologetic for his Anders Frisk and Eva Carneiro excesses now than at the time. Yet Mourinho also articulates his desire to be loved, though you sometimes wonder if, to him, that has as much in common with adulation as affection. “It can also be: ‘I want to have a lot of attention on me’,” says Pearlman, “and conflict brings that in spades. It’s like this safety blanket that allows him to feel like he’s doing things for a righteous cause.”

At home Mourinho is different: more reserved, quieter. And it is with regard to his home life that we experience the show’s other sad moment: Mourinho explaining he’s been away from his family a lot, so much so that it’s easier for them when he’s not around. “You can kind of hear it in my voice,” says Pearlman. “I’m like: ‘Oh my god, what does it even feel like saying that?’”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

What does Pearlman think the show is about? “A lot of it is about winning at all costs,” he replies, “and what happens when you’re defined by winning and that winning stops. It’s also the portrait of a hero and a villain, one of the great leaders of men that the world has ever seen. As a civilisation, we’re lucky Mourinho didn’t go into politics!”

And, of course, the show now has a surprise happy ending, with Mourinho’s return to Madrid. “The person I’ve seen over the last few years at Roma, Benfica … until this last one, I don’t think I could say that I’ve met a happy man or a content person,” says Pearlman. “He is now where he believes he should always have been – after every cup Madrid have won since he left, Florentino Pérez has called to say: ‘This is because of you,’ because of how he modernised the club. And one thing we all know is that whatever comes next, it’s going to be a box-office blockbuster.”

Sports.title: From Fenerbahce to Drita: six European ties to check out this week
Sports.content:
Champions League

Fenerbahce v Lyon, Tuesday 8pm

Romelu Lukaku is the latest familiar face to rock up at Fenerbahce. The 33-year-old striker is, however, unlikely to be fit for Lyon’s visit to Istanbul on Tuesday – he sat out Saturday’s 2-1 defeat to Genclerbirligi, the club his father played for in the 1990s. “This beautiful country is a second home to me,” Lukaku, who spent part of his childhood in Turkey, said last week. Fenerbahce have also added Mason Greenwood and Nathan Aké to a squad that includes Ederson, N’Golo Kanté and Marco Asensio. Failure to get past Lyon, who are aiming to qualify for the Champions League for the first time since reaching the semi-finals in 2019-20, would not be the best start to Ismail Kartal’s fourth spell as head coach.

Celtic v LASK, Wednesday 8pm

Even before seeing Rangers and Hearts suffer damaging qualifying defeats this summer, Celtic would have needed no reminding of how much jeopardy these ties contain. Kairat Almaty dumped Brendan Rodgers’ side out at this stage last season on penalties after two goalless draws. “They are big games in every aspect … prestige, finance,” said Martin O’Neill, who will have grim memories of his own defeat to Basel in the playoffs 24 years ago. In both legs against LASK, the Austrian champions, Celtic will have to do without Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain as the midfielder serves a three-match ban for a red card he received playing for Besiktas in the Conference League in 2023.

Europa League

Trabzonspor v Ferencvaros, Thursday 6pm

Mohamed Salah could make his home debut for Trabzonspor when they take on Ferencvaros in Turkey. The former Liverpool forward came off the bench – along with Cape Verde’s Sidny Lopes Cabral – in the second half of Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Kasimpasa. Ferencvaros will not be overawed by the occasion, with a glamour friendly against Real Madrid in Budapest part of their pre-season preparations. Among the ranks of last season’s Hungarian Cup winners, who replaced Robbie Keane with Balazs Borbely in the dugout this summer, is Salah’s former Liverpool teammate Naby Keïta. They have been to Serbia, the Netherlands and Poland in three rounds of Europa League qualifying so far.

Egnatia v Lillestrøm, Thursday 6pm

Hans Erik Ødegaard, father of Arsenal’s Premier League-winning captain Martin, has been working miracles in his two years in charge of Lillestrøm. After being appointed head coach following the Norwegian side’s relegation in 2024, he oversaw their immediate return to the top flight unbeaten and won the Norwegian Cup in the process. Ødegaard, who coached in Real Madrid’s academy after his son’s move there in 2015, will lead Lillestrøm into their first European main draw since the Uefa Cup in 2000-01 as defeat would still guarantee them a Conference League place. Egnatia are the Albanian champions from the past three years and overturned a 3-1 deficit to Shamrock Rovers in the previous round.

Conference League

Tromsø v Brighton, Thursday 6pm

Sussex is officially in drought but Brighton supporters will have to dig out their coats if they are making the trip to Europe’s most northern football club. It is forecast to be 13C and raining by the time Fabian Hürzeler’s side kick off in Tromsø, situated over 200 miles into the Arctic Circle. Jørgen Vik’s team have dropped down from Europa League qualifying but are looking to make the most of home advantage against Premier League opposition. “Facing our style of play on artificial turf could potentially come as a shock to them,” said Vik. Tromsø and Lillestrøm are two of five Eliteserien teams involved in European playoffs this week. “There is a great deal of confidence in Norwegian football right now,” said Vik.

Drita v Inter Club d’Escaldes, Thursday 7pm

Since winning their first Andorran league title in 2020, Inter Club d’Escaldes, who wear black and blue stripes like the Italian Inter, have fallen short in six European qualifying campaigns, but this is the first time they have been one round away. Inter are coached by Felip Ortiz, a former goalkeeper who shared a flat with Carles Puyol when they were teenagers at Barcelona, and they will be no pushovers having put six without reply past Flora Tallinn in the previous round. Drita, the reigning champions of Kosovo who reached the knockout stage of last season’s Conference League, stand in Inter’s way of making history.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Atlético want Alvarez to join Arsenal over Barça?
Sports.content:
A new Premier League season is only days away, so it stands to reason that a few clubs are getting panicky in the transfer market. Newcastle are certainly in need of some fresh faces after being raided earlier in the summer so, after being linked with Christopher Nkunku, could move for RB Leipzig midfielder Nicolas Seiwald. The Austria international played under Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Newcastle have shunned Manchester United’s attempts to snare Lewis Hall, so the Old Trafford club are still in the market for a left-back. Joaquin Seys, 21, of Club Brugge, is said to be a carbon copy of Hall and the Belgian has apparently been shunted to the top of United’s hitlist. The Barcelona midfielder Marc Casadó is also a potential United midfield target with the Catalan club ready to move on the 22-year-old after agreeing a deal for Rodri.

Let’s stay in Spain for a moment, where the future of Julián Alvarez has been a hot topic all summer. The former Manchester City forward remains keen to join Barcelona, but Atlético Madrid are understandably a bit edgy about selling their best player to a domestic rival. It seems Atléti would prefer him to go to Arsenal. A meeting between Miguel Ángel Gil Marín, the club’s chief suit, and Alvarez is scheduled, where the latter’s future will be thrashed out. Stand by, Gunners fans.

Liverpool have danced with Bradley Barcola all summer and now want another Paris Saint-Germain winger in the shape of 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye. A combined fee of £155m has been mooted for the pair. Manchester United are possible Mbaye suitors, too, along with a number of others.

Leeds have done some solid business this summer and are now interested in Nelson Deossa from Real Betis. The midfielder, along with Marseille wide man Igor Paixão, is on the Whites’ radar, though it’s claimed Paixão could be lured by the riches of the Saudi Pro League instead. Zian Flemming from Burnley is another possibility, though he could cost nearly £20m, as Leeds look to replace the West Ham-bound Joël Piroe.

View image in fullscreen Igor Paixão in pre-season action for Marseille against Atlético Madrid last week. Photograph: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

One Championship player on the move may be Blackburn goalkeeper Balazs Toth. The £4m-rated Hungarian international is wanted by Celtic as a Kasper Schmeichel replacement. Rangers, meanwhile, are set to finalise the transfer of Aston Villa defender Kosta Nedeljkovic, and also want to add Kevin Kelsy, a striker for Venezuela and Portland Timbers. Rangers desperately need a transfer boost or two, that’s for sure.

And finally, could Jamie Vardy be set for a final hurrah in Brazil? West Ham had previously been linked with the former Leicester striker, who is still a free agent after leaving Cremonese, but São Paulo may enter the market for the 39-year-old.

Sports.title: Guardiola’s row with Walker at Manchester City revealed in new Amazon documentary
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola clashed with his captain and almost broke down in tears as he railed at players during his worst run as Manchester City manager.

Guardiola stood down at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. One of the lowest points of his glittering reign came during a testing run in the autumn of 2024, when City lost nine times and won only once in 13 games. Guardiola outwardly showed signs of strain, notably when he scratched his face after City surrendered a 3-0 lead to draw 3-3 with Feyenoord in the Champions League.

Behind closed doors he was also angry and upset with his players, as shown in a new fly-on-the-wall Amazon Prime documentary, A Beautiful Obsession.

At one point he argued in the dressing room with then captain Kyle Walker, who felt he was being unfairly singled out. “You keep saying my name in every meeting,” complained Walker after a defeat at Liverpool. “Every fucking meeting it’s my name. You’ve somehow brought my name into it.”

Walker, who had been voted captain by his teammates, also claimed Guardiola did not want him to be skipper.

Guardiola responded by saying Walker was taking the issue too personally but also showed signs of emotion as he explained why he had extended his contract despite their poor run.

“If I am a problem you have to tell me,” said Guardiola in a broken voice. “I won’t stay here for the money or just for the fact of staying. I extended my contract because I want to be with you. I want to fight. I don’t want you to feel like I’m leaving or running away.”

View image in fullscreen Pep Guardiola speaking to Kyle Walker when Manchester City played Spurs in November 2024. The two clashed when Walker was captain. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Reuters

Another extraordinary outburst came in November 2025 after a dismal 2-0 loss to Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League. Guardiola, whose decision to make 10 changes had backfired, threatened to quit in the dressing room afterwards.

He said: “It’s unacceptable this lack of courage, passion and love and desire to win and do it better. I work for you. I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away, and everything for all of you. And what do you give back? The fucking performance you have done. It’s a disgrace guys. I’m really fucking tired. When I see that I’m exhausted, I’m drained. I want to quit.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the Manchester City chair, recently said Guardiola must have threatened to leave “100 times” during his tenure but he too had his concerns after the Leverkusen game.

In a remarkable release of voice notes between Khaldoon and the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, the chair said he was “so angry” after “probably one of the lowest points we’ve had”. Soriano said the response should not be “too negative or aggressive” but “not too kind or accommodating either”.

The four-part series, which covers the past two seasons, also includes some frank boardroom discussions about transfer policy and the long-serving Kevin De Bruyne’s disappointment after being told his contract would not be renewed.

Sports.title: Four Chelsea players who could leave before window closes as Enzo Fernandez deadline day drama predicted
Sports.content:
Four Chelsea players who could leave before window closes as Enzo Fernandez deadline day drama predicted

Chelsea could be set for a lively end to the transfer window with the futures of four players still to be decided.

Boss Xabi Alonso is in the process of navigating through his bloated squad to find his trusted XI ahead of the new season.

4 Alonso still has plenty of work to do in reshaping his squad ahead of the Premier League season Credit: Getty

That will inevitably be a brutal process for the Spaniard who is tasked with informing multiple stars that their services will not be required this season.

Whilst the door remains open for potential new incomings this summer, talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook says trimming the squad is the club’s priority in the final weeks of the window, which closes on September 1.

“I think the focus is on getting players out at this moment in time,” Crook told talkSPORT before revealing which players are most likely to depart.

Who could leave Chelsea this summer?

“Keep an eye on Liam Delap, £40million bounty on his head as I understand it,” he added.

“Nicolas Jackson is another who could potentially move on. Axel Disasi has got interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.”

Vice-captain Enzo Fernandez remains the most high profile name that could leave the club this month.

The Argentine has communicated his desire to leave the club with his preferred destination being a move to Real Madrid.

The LaLiga club quickly poured cold water on a move last month leaving the midfielder in limbo.

Manchester City have been strongly linked with a move for the 25-years-old but failed to submit an offer by Chelsea’s set deadline of 5pm last Friday.

And whilst speculation has briefly quietened down in recent days, Crook believes there is still life in the deal and predicts a blockbuster deadline day for the Argentine.

4 Newcastle, Everton and Nottingham Forest have all been linked with Delap in recent days Credit: Getty

4 Fernandez recently returned to Chelsea training following his eventful World Cup with Argentina Credit: Getty

Will there be late drama in the Fernandez deal?

“We’re going to be talking a lot about Enzo Fernandez in the next couple of weeks,” he said.

“I can see a repeat scenario of when he came from Benfica where we get to deadline day and Manchester City are trying to get that deal done.

“I think that might be the big story of deadline day.”

Fernandez returned to action for the Blues in Saturday’s 3-1 pre-season friendly win over Real Sociedad.

Introduced as a second-half substitute, Fernandez received a mixed reception from the Stamford Bridge faithful.

Sections of the Chelsea support have been angered by the star’s repeated attempts to angle for a move to Real Madrid.

4 Fernandez was given a mixed reception on his return to action on Saturday Credit: Getty

Others were left disappointed by his antics in Argentina’s 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England last month where Fernandez netted his country’s equaliser late on.

Fernandez joined Chelsea in a £106.8m deal from Benfica in January 2023.

He has since clocked up 169 appearances for the west London club, scoring 31 goals and providing 30 assists during that time.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho could use Gareth Southgate blueprint to fix Real Madrid dilemma
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has been urged to use Trent Alexander-Arnold in a new role at Real Madrid this season.

It comes as he faces a key selection dilemma ahead of their opening fixture.



4 Mourinho has been urged to move Alexander-Arnold into midfield this season Credit: Getty

Alexander-Arnold enjoyed an impressive debut campaign with the Spanish giants last term.

The right-back joined the club from Liverpool in June 2025 before going on to make 35 appearances across all competitions.

Despite missing three months through injury, he was still able to provide seven assists from defence.



Mourinho has continued to deploy Alexander-Arnold in his usual right-back role during pre-season.

However, European football journalist Andy Brassell believes the 27-year-old could be the solution to Real Madrid's midfield headache.



With former target Rodri joining Barcelona for £65million, Mourinho's side have been left looking light in the centre of the park.

Outside of Aurelien Tchouameni, Federico Valverde and Eduardo Camavinga, his options appear weak in the position.



Position change for Alexander-Arnold?

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, Brassell has proposed using Alexander-Arnold to bolster their midfield.

He explained: "I think trying him out there, there's nothing wrong with it.

"Especially after the Rodri move fell through and they do need someone with vision at the base of the midfield. There's no doubt about that.

4 Mourinho is facing a selection headache in midfield ahead of the new season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"Not comparing Alexander-Arnold to Rodri at all, but they're looking for someone to do that sort of job.

"I do think the player they need in that spot is not necessarily a £150million glamour signing. I think it's someone who will probably just do a pretty basic brutal job for them.

"Now, maybe Tchouameni can be that guy. Maybe Trent Alexander-Arnold can be that guy. But the link that has been made between them and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, for example, I understand that.

"He's definitely a Mourinho type of guy. Massive personality. Doesn't mind getting his hands dirty. Technically a lot better than people would like to admit.



"Of course, he was a playmaker when he came through at Bayern. He's a bit of a favourite of Pep Guardiola, ironically. So that would make a lot of sense."

Alexander-Arnold was often used in midfield by former England manager Gareth Southgate during his tenure.

4 Southgate regularly used Alexander-Arnold in midfield for England Credit: Getty

He most notably featured in the role during Euro 2024, with three of his four appearances coming as a central midfielder.



However, Alexander-Arnold has yet to appear in the middle of the park since signing for Real Madrid last summer.

Who will be Real Madrid's starting right-back?

Brassell admits the availability of new signing Denzel Dumfries could also be a factor in a potential change of role for Alexander-Arnold.

The Netherlands international will compete with Alexander-Arnold at right-back following his arrival from Inter Milan.

Brassell continued: "I think before fully committing to a Trent Alexander-Arnold experiment in midfield, I think really we have to know that (Denzel) Dumfries can play all the games because he's had a few injuries over the last couple of seasons.



"Inter obviously still didn't want to lose him, but I think it makes it kind of easier to move on. It feels as if Djed Spence is younger, he's going to be more available. That feels like a good thing for Inter to me.

4 Alexander-Arnold has exclusively featured at right-back for Real Madrid during pre-season Credit: Getty

"I don't think that Dumfries arriving necessarily means that Trent Alexander-Arnold is not going to get any Madrid games this season. I don't think that's the case at all.

"Also, we have to go back and say when he was available last season, he was really, really good as well. He added a different dimension to Real Madrid and the way they played.



"Now if you can bring that into midfield, maybe that's something else again.

"I think if you're talking about initiating quick transitions, making the most of Vinicius Jr, of (Kylian) Mbappe, of (Yan) Diomande, Trent Alexander-Arnold's passing at the base of that midfield could be super useful for that.

"So it's an experiment that I would very much like to see."

Real Madrid begin their LaLiga campaign away to Espanyol on Saturday, Mourinho's first competitive match since returning as manager on a three-year deal.

Sports.title: Patrick Vieira returns to football with first international job after ten months without a gig
Sports.content:
Patrick Vieira returns to football with first international job after ten months without a gig

Patrick Vieira has been announced as the new head coach of Senegal.

It marks the Arsenal and France legend's return to management after leaving Genoa last November.

2 Vieira steered Genoa to Serie A safety in 2024/25 Credit: Getty

A new chapter for Vieira

Vieira succeeds Pape Thiaw, who was sacked by the Lions of Teranga following their World Cup last-16 exit this summer.

And the 50-year-old has a special connection to Senegal: although he ultimately earned 107 caps for France, winning the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000, he was born in the Senegalese capital, Dakar.

This will be the iconic former midfielder's sixth frontline coaching role – and his first in international football.

Widely regarded as one of the finest midfielders of all time, Vieira won three Premier League titles with Arsene Wenger's Arsenal, captaining them to glory in the famous 'Invincibles' season of 2003/04.

He later won three Serie A titles and the Champions League with Inter Milan.

Having retired from playing in 2011 after a short spell with Manchester City, winning the FA Cup in one of his final career appearances, Vieira went on to manage the club's Elite Development Squad.

He subsequently took charge of New York City and Nice before returning to the Premier League as Crystal Palace boss in 2021.

Dismissed by Palace towards the end of the 2022/23 season, Vieira then took charge at Strasbourg and Genoa.

Vieira follows in France teammates' footsteps

The three-time Premier League champion is the latest member of France's victorious 1998 World Cup squad to take the reins of a national team.

Captain Didier Deschamps became only the third person to win the World Cup as a player and manager when he led Les Bleus' to their second crown in 2018.

2 Vieira led Crystal Palace to 12th place in the Premier League in 2021/22 Credit: Getty

Having succeeded Laurent Blanc in 2012, he stood down after this summer's tournament to be succeeded by another of his old teammates, Zinedine Zidane.

Additionally, Thierry Henry coached France to silver at the 2024 Olympics in Paris, and goalkeeper Bernard Lama briefly managed Kenya.

Senegal set their sights on AFCON

Vieira's first mission in his new job will be to guide Senegal to qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

The Lions of Teranga were crowned continental champions for the first time at the 2021 edition and thought they had lifted the trophy again last time around, only for Morocco to be awarded the title by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) – who overturned the result following a hugely controversial final in which Senegal left the pitch in protest at refereeing decisions.

Qualifying for the 2027 AFCON begins next month, with Senegal hosting Mozambique then travelling to Ethiopia.

Sudan are the other nation in the Lions of Teranga's four-team group.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos consortium has route to full Liverpool ownership as new clause revealed
Sports.content:
Jeff Bezos consortium has route to full Liverpool ownership as new clause revealed

Liverpool could have new controlling owners within a year.

The Reds had a shake-up at the top last Friday when a consortium, which included Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, purchased a minority share in the club from incumbent owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).

2 Liverpool represents Bezos' first foray into sports ownership Credit: Getty

Initial reports stated the consortium's stake was around 30 per cent.

How Jeff Bezos' consortium can take over Liverpool

However, talkSPORT understands it is instead higher than that.

The consortium, titled 1892 Holdings and fronted by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia, bought a stake estimated to be 38 per cent.

It is also understood that an option for 1892 Holdings to purchase a controlling stake in Liverpool was included as part of the terms outlined in the agreement with FSG.

The option can be taken up in the next 12 months and is not controlled by FSG.

"Liverpool has always been built by thinking beyond one season and making decisions with the club's long-term interests in mind," FSG president Mike Gordon said upon confirming 1892 Holdings' investment.

"That approach continues to attract interest from respected investors and business leaders around the world.

"As we considered this opportunity, it became clear that Amit and the consortium shared our long-term philosophy and appreciation for what makes Liverpool special.

"Their experience and perspective will complement the strong foundation already in place, and we look forward to working together."

What has Liverpool won in the FSG era?

FSG purchased Liverpool in 2010 for £298million and have overseen plenty of success.

2 Under FSG, Liverpool ended their 30-year wait to win the English top flight Credit: AFP

Since the 2018/19 campaign, the Reds have won an impressive eight trophies.

The silverware haul includes two Premier League titles, the FA Cup, two Carabao Cups, the Champions League, the Super Cup and the Club World Cup.

Liverpool will look to add more trophies to their collection this season as they embark on a new era led by Andoni Iraola.

Iraola was appointed as Arne Slot's successor following the Dutchman's axing after just two seasons.

The ex-Cherries boss has already overseen a number of key transfers, with winger Victor Munoz joining from Osasuna while defender Ronald Araujo signed from Barcelona on a season-long loan.

Liverpool commence the 2026/27 Premier League season on Sunday away at Newcastle, with kick-off scheduled for 4:30pm.

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli already has perfect transfer destination after rejecting Galatasaray move
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli has been told that he could be more productive than anyone could imagine if he joins the right club this summer.

talkSPORT revealed on Sunday that the Arsenal star is expected to leave the club before the end of the transfer window.



3 Martinelli was a notable absentee from Arsenal's Community Shield squad Credit: Getty

Martinelli was left out of the Gunners' 20-man squad for the 3-0 Community Shield victory over FA Cup holders Manchester City.

The Brazilian was previously the subject of interest from Galatasaray, who followed up their initial enquiry with a £38.4million verbal offer.

However, Martinelli, who has scored 62 goals in 278 games for Arsenal, informed the club that he doesn't want to join the Turkish giants.



Gabriel Martinelli to Roma transfer

European football expert Andy Brassell has now tipped Italian giants Roma as a potential landing spot for the 25-year-old Brazil forward.

"I think straight away there's one club that pops up," he exclusively told talkSPORT.com of Martinelli's immediate future.



"They've been looking for wide players all summer. You've had Premier League players who've sort of lost their way, resurrect their careers in Italy, not just English players but Premier League players.

"I think Roma is a good spot for him. I think he'd be great there.

"He'd have a greater level of importance than he does at Arsenal. Price-wise, that maybe is an issue."



Roma have already completed a rejuvenation project with a versatile forward who found himself a fringe player at a Premier League club.

3 Martinelli was one of three absentees against City who are the subject of transfer speculation Credit: Getty

Donyell Malen left Aston Villa to join the Giallorossi in January on an initial loan spell after becoming a bit-part winger under Unai Emery.

Trusted with leading the line in Italy, the Dutchman scored 14 goals in 18 Serie A appearances and has now completed a permanent switch.



Ironically, Emery was Arsenal manager when Martinelli arrived in north London, and first learnt his trade as a striker.

Brassell added that a fresh start at Roma could provide him with the impetus needed to restart that development as a key source of goals.

"I think with the right club, Martinelli could be more productive than anyone could imagine," he added to talkSPORT.

"At the moment at least, he seems to have been scaled down to what is basically a deluxe sub the last little while.



3 Martinelli scored just one Premier League goal en route to Arsenal lifting the title last season Credit: Getty

Gabriel Martinelli PL goals by season at Arsenal 2025/26 - 1 2024/25 - 8 2023/24 - 6 2022/23 - 15 2021/22 - 6

Roma would also be a good spot for Marcus Rashford

"I can understand that because Arsenal have moved on to a very high level of course," Brassell continued.

"But we can't forget that he started out as a centre-forward before moving on to the wing.

"I think in the right club he can get a lot of goals.

"I think he'd do very, very well at Roma if they were able to find the funds. As you know, I think that would be a good spot for Marcus Rashford. That's probably an even more difficult deal to do because of the wages.



"But yeah, they're still in the market for wide players. So that is one that I think would be really interesting."

Sports.title: ‘Worst signing’ Nick Woltemade could be offered shock lifeline at Champions League club
Sports.content:
Nick Woltemade has been tipped to complete a sensational loan switch to Como as he looks to revive his career.

The German striker endured a difficult first season at Newcastle following his club-record £69million move from Stuttgart last summer.



5 Woltemade was Newcastle's club-record signing from VfB Stuttgart last summer Credit: Getty

After scoring four goals in his first five Premier League games, Woltemade then suffered a dip in form.

The 24-year-old went on to net just four more times in the league last term, only one of which came in 2026.

Woltemade's struggles saw him face some stinging criticism, including being branded the worst signing in Premier League history.



His woes came in a trying season for Newcastle collectively, as they finished a disappointing 12th - with manager Eddie Howe since departing St James' Park amid a summer exodus.

Serie A switch?

With Woltemade struggling to make his mark in his first year in English football, it remains to be seen whether he will be given a second chance under new Newcastle boss Mathias Jaissle.



With fellow summer signing Yoane Wissa also enduring a tough 2025/26 season, Will Osula could lead the line this term.

And European football expert Andy Brassell believes Woltemade could get back up and running under Cesc Fabregas at Como.



The Serie A side are gearing up for their first-ever Champions League campaign, and Brassell believes they could turn to the German to strengthen their forward line, with Alvaro Morata signing permanently despite netting just once last season.

He told talkSPORT.com: “The bottom line is they need a Morata replacement, because they spent a lot of last summer trying to piece together this deal for Alvaro Morata, and it hasn't worked out."

Highlighting Como's need for a striker, Brassell continued: “They clearly need an upgrade or at least some assistance.

5 Woltemade was dropped to the bench for a period last season amid his ongoing struggles Credit: Alamy



5 Alvaro Morata has endured a tough time at Como since initially joining on loan from AC Milan last summer Credit: Getty

"Because they're going into the Champions League as well, which is earlier than they expected. But they're going to need to beef up that squad.

“So an interesting one, if we're looking at loans from the Premier League. I wonder if Nick Woltemade would suit them, actually.

“Now I'm sure that if it doesn't work out medium term for Woltemade at Newcastle, I think Bayern Munich will probably make it happen at some point, because I think it's clear there's a really good player there.



“Whether Matthias Jaissle is going to make a team that suits Woltemade, I think is a bit of a question mark over still."

Shot at redemption

Brassell had doubts over whether Woltemade will be given a chance to prove himself under Jaissle at Newcastle, insisting Wissa and Osula are likely ahead of him in the pecking order.

Wissa looked back to his best at this summer's World Cup with three goals in four games for DR Congo, while Osula netted an impressive five goals in Newcastle's final seven league games last term.

5 Woltemade showcased his attacking prowess at the start of last season, getting off to a strong start in English football Credit: Getty



Discussing what would be best for Woltemade, Brassell felt an initial loan move was most likely if Newcastle are to try and recoup his huge £59m transfer fee.

And he believes Fabregas could be just the man to improve his game, with the ex-Premier League star earning a strong reputation at Como.

He said: “I think there has to be a question about Woltemade.

“What's clear as well is that Newcastle can't really sell him tomorrow. Because they're going to take a massive loss on him if they were to do that. If they were to decide that they wanted to move on and he wasn't the fit for them.

“So really, I think loaning him to somewhere where he could be worked on with a coach who's got a bit of vision, who's super intelligent and who's good at developing players.



“Because Woltemade is still a young player. He's still under 25. I think we can forget that - that he's meant to be a project."

5 Since taking charge of Como in 2024, Cesc Fabregas has guided the club to a best-ever Serie A season in 2025/26, finishing fourth Credit: Getty

Outlining how Fabregas could help him, Brassell explained: “I think he would benefit a lot from being coached by Cesc Fabregas as well, who is someone who also really emphasises the defensive part of the game.

“Now I personally think I haven't watched Woltemade a lot first hand since he's arrived at Newcastle - I think he's learnt to press better.



“There's a lot on his game that could be worked on to turn him into a really great player still, I'm just losing a bit of faith that Newcastle is necessarily the right place to do that. I hope they can get him to work it out, but I'm not 100 per cent sure that they can.

“So if we're looking for a value loan of a player who could still become elite level.

"I think that's an interesting one for Como to look at if they could make something work.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard told Coventry’s new £21m signing could become ‘properly special’
Sports.content:
Anticipated Coventry City signing Sidiki Cherif has 'enormous potential' and could be the perfect fit for the Premier League newcomers.

That's the view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who believes the sky's the limit for the 19-year-old striker widely reported to be joining Frank Lampard's Sky Blues.

2 Cherif scored twice in 10 Turkish Super Lig appearances for Fenerbahce last season Credit: Getty

Cherif previously came through the youth ranks at French club Angers.

And Brassell thinks a move to Coventry would suit both parties.

Cherif 'really good' at Fenerbahce

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT about Sidiki, he said: "He's still young. There's a lot of pressure to put on him. He's not got the history of scoring 20 goals a season because he just hasn't been around for long enough.

"But he looked the part at Angers and he arrived at Fenerbahce in winter last season and looked like he was going to be back up to another big centre-forward. They never got that other big centre-forward.

"He ended up playing a lot more than you thought he would. But he was good; he was really good. Someone like that who is really good at holding the ball up, who can score goals... He's intelligent; he can run the channels – but he's also good with the ball in front of him.

"That's really ideal if you're Coventry. He can play a lot of different ways. Despite being young, he's not fazed by big pressure situations. He'll get time and good coaching.

"So I feel like it's a pretty good move for him. It's another example of how Premier League money can make a massive difference and enable clubs that you wouldn't think would be able to to get in players that you wouldn't think they would be able to get."

Brassell went on to explain what a high ceiling Cherif has and what a top player he could become.

He continued: "He's got enormous potential; there's no doubt about it. He's shown already, I think in a relatively small sample size, that he's got the ability to step up and really take the bull by the horns. This is a great opportunity for him.

"Clearly the way Fenerbahce have gone is a bit more experienced. They've brought in Romelu Lukaku as well. Maybe that would limit his minutes a little bit. But Cherif scored [and] showed in big moments last season that he was ready to seize the opportunity with both hands.

"So, if you think that Angers were written off left and right; they've had some horrendous financial problems over the last couple of years. He was a big part of them punching way above their weight before he went last season. So I guess in that sense, it's a similar situation to Coventry. No one's expecting them to stay up.

2 Born in Guinea, Cherif was called up to the France Under-21 squad earlier this year Credit: Getty

"I think he's a really good get. I think coach him right and he could turn into something properly special."

Coventry's busy summer

Last season's Championship winners, Coventry have already made a host of signings as they head into their first top-flight campaign for 25 years.

Remarkably, the Sky Blues have broken their transfer record four times during the current window, most recently to bring in Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi from Danish side Nordsjaelland.

Their latest new signing arrived on Monday as striker Taiwo Awoniyi joined from Nottingham Forest.

However, they have reportedly had a bid for Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who Lampard managed at Chelsea, turned down by AC Milan.

Sky Blues face big challenge on long-awaited return

Coventry begin the new season with the toughest test possible: a trip to champions Arsenal for Friday's Premier League curtain-raiser, live on talkSPORT.

The Sky Blues then host fellow promoted team Hull City in their first home game the following Saturday.







﻿

Sports.title: Inside story of Aston Villa's summer: Why club dug heels in with Arsenal over Morgan Rogers, the Alejandro Garnacho loan explained, new £38m sponsor deals boosting the 'brand', the Villa Park revamp gamble and deals that could still be done
Sports.content:
Aston Villa may have lost several key men from their march to European glory but at least the guy who made it all happen is still in place.

Unai Emery is arguably the club’s greatest manager of modern times. He may not have won the league title like Ron Saunders or lifted the European Cup like Tony Barton, but in less than four years at the helm he has transformed Villa into a serious force – against substantial odds.

Villa dread the day Emery leaves and though there was never any serious possibility of him doing so this summer, there were a few jitters around the club’s Bodymoor Heath training ground last spring. When it appeared briefly that Diego Simeone and Atletico Madrid might part ways, Emery looked the ideal replacement.

His reputation in Spain remains very high, and Atletico’s director of football Mateu Alemany is a huge admirer. Alemany, remember, was on the point of becoming Villa’s president of football operations in spring 2023, only to back out at the last minute. One day, Simeone will leave Atletico and if Alemany is still in place, Emery will be high on his list.

Happily for Villa fans, they do not have to worry about that today. Yet what should have been a summer of celebration and consolidation turned into one of transition – as Emery always suspected it would.

Villa’s wrangles with UEFA financial rules have been discussed at length. This summer, it has meant one in, one out, with the £117million sale of Morgan Rogers driving the process.

Aston Villa may have lost several key men from their march to European glory but at least manager Unai Emery is still in place

The sale of Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for £117m has shaped the whole summer for Villa

Rogers’ record departure

Even when they agreed a new six-year deal with Rogers last November, Emery and his key lieutenants knew it would likely be their star attacker’s last season at Villa Park.

Villa were facing an uphill struggle to comply with UEFA spending rules and Rogers was the one asset able to ease those problems at a stroke. There was interest from across the Premier League and from Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, too, but Rogers’ next club boiled down quickly to two: Arsenal or Chelsea.

The Gunners were the obvious choice. Newly-crowned Premier League champions and Champions League finalists, Mikel Arteta’s men were a hugely attractive option.

During England’s World Cup preparations, it is thought Rogers was sounded out by the Arsenal players in Thomas Tuchel’s squad. There were also discreet meetings between Rogers’ advisers and representatives working for Arsenal. The signs were positive.

Yet one thing was missing. While he was willing to let Rogers leave, Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris had studied the market and seen Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali given price tags of £100million and more. He was already irked by the idea that Arsenal might offer only £30million for Ezri Konsa when Villa value him at twice that. Why should he allow Rogers to leave on the cheap?

Arsenal had made Rogers their first choice but were unwilling to go above £80million, confident Rogers’ desire to join them would see the deal done in the end. How wrong they were.

It is unclear exactly when Chelsea sealed the Rogers deal but Daily Mail Sport has learned that at least a fortnight before the transfer was announced, the 24-year-old was very confident he would be heading to Stamford Bridge.

There are excellent relations between Sawiris and the leaders of BlueCo, who own Chelsea, and that undoubtedly helped the transfer and paved the way for Alejandro Garnacho to move to Villa Park on loan. Garnacho will join Villa permanently if he hits certain targets and could still be followed by Nicolas Jackson in the closing hours of the window.

Villa have a good relationship with Chelsea which paved the way for Alejandro Garnacho to move to Villa Park on loan

Could Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson be on his way to Villa too?

With Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne also leaving for Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, Villa are under no pressure to sell any more stars, though fringe players like Leon Bailey and – possibly – Tammy Abraham may leave.

Konsa’s future remains a doubt while there has been interest in Ollie Watkins, too, though neither would leave before high-level replacements are secured.

Zion Suzuki is set to join Villa from Parma for £30million and will become Villa's first-choice goalkeeper, despite Emi Martinez's move to Juventus collapsing.

Villa have taken a risk with Johan Manzambi. Buying any player while he is injured is far from ideal, certainly not for a £52million record fee. Manzambi’s knee injury, sustained at the World Cup, was significant and Villa must hope there are no lingering effects when he eventually returns to action.

Off the pitch

After Emery, the most important figure at Villa is Francesco Calvo. Operating with the rather grand title of ‘president of business operations’, the Italian’s job is to grow revenue. Fast.

The summer has been tough and the coming months promise to be equally challenging, though Calvo is working impressively.

By offering front-of-shirt space to new sponsors Visit Rwanda, where wealthier clubs were proposing only sleeve space, Calvo managed to win the race and secure a £20million-a-year investment – easily the largest in Villa’s history.

Arsenal received significant backlash for their sleeve partnership with Visit Rwanda, which ended in 2025, and Villa were braced for something similar. In June, the Democratic Republic of Congo filed a case against Rwanda at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), accusing its neighbour of breaching multiple international treaties.

Amnesty International have raised concerns yet compared with Arsenal’s deal, the reaction to Villa’s arrangement has been relatively mild.

Villa sealed a £20million-a-year sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, while last season’s front-of-shirt partner Betano will now have their name on the Villa sleeve

On top of the Visit Rwanda package, last season’s front-of-shirt partner Betano will now have their name displayed on the sleeve. That is worth an additional £18million over three years.

Apart from selling their best players, Villa’s only way to catch up with richer rivals is by improving their commercial status. Sustained improvement under Emery has made Villa a better ‘brand’, as the Spaniard put it ahead of the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain. Now the challenge is to bring more people through the door – another key item on Calvo’s to-do list.

New Villa Park

Formerly of Juventus and Barcelona, Calvo is ambitious. He is pushing ahead with a plan to increase Villa Park’s capacity to 50,000, starting from next season. The catch is that the North Stand will be closed this term, reducing the capacity to 37,000.

Trying to turn around a major building project in a little more than a year is brave. Liverpool needed nearly four years to complete the Anfield Road Stand. What happens if works run behind schedule, as they often do? Just ask anyone who has ever attempted even a minor renovation at home.

Emery has always had nagging fears about reduced capacity. The Villa boss was instrumental in shelving former CEO Christian Purslow’s redevelopment plans as he feared it would have too great an impact on home form.

If he is worried about it again, then he should look at Tottenham, who played at reduced capacity in their last season at White Hart Lane in 2016-17 and promptly won 17 of their 19 home games, drawing the other two.

Calvo is juggling numerous balls here. He is actively seeking a naming-rights deal but given the history behind Villa Park, must choose carefully. The North Stand project means 5,000 supporters will not sit in their usual seats this term.

Villa Park's North Stand will be closed this season, reducing capacity to 37,000 as the club try to increase the number of fans they can accommodate in the following season

On top of that, there is growing discontent about ticket prices and those voices may grow louder when the Champions League packages are announced.

Yet Calvo is in a tough spot here. Villa need to boost revenue and the temptation is to pull every lever to do so. There is a certain point, though, when fans will say ‘Enough’. The Villa Park atmosphere felt flat at times last season and that should worry everyone at the club.

If Calvo can emulate off the pitch what Emery has achieved on it, the future will stay rosy for Villa. It may prove an even more challenging job for the Italian than his colleague in the dugout.

Sports.title: Vicario joins Juventus on loan, Newcastle complete £29.5m signing of Amar Dedic while Everton chief urges calm as club hunt for right-back: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Sociedad want West Ham's Edson

Real Sociedad have followed up their interest in West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Mexico international also had interest from former club Ajax but is keen to move to La Liga and talks are ongoing.

One Hull of an offer for Garcia

Hull City have offered around £4.5million for Real Betis forward Pablo Garcia as talks continue over a deal.

As Daily Mail Sport reported at the weekend, Hull turned to the highly-rated 20-year-old winger after talks for Leon Bailey fell through. Betis want at least £7m and a substantial sell-on.

Hull have also asked about Yeremay Hernandez at Deportivo Coruna and been offered Keito Nakamura from Reims.

Pablo Garcia in pre-season action against Arsenal earlier this month

Stoke want to seal deal for Hirst

Stoke City have revived talks for Ipswich Town striker George Hirst in the hope of signing him by the weekend. Stoke travel to Southampton on Saturday.

Betis progress on Parrott after West Ham bid rejected

Real Betis are making progress in talks with AZ Alkmaar over a deal for striker Troy Parrott.

West Ham had an initial £15m bid rejected and were expected to go back but talks with Alkmaar have proved difficult.

The Hammers have since moved to finalise a loan for Leeds striker Joel Piroe.

Betis could be helped in their pursuit of Parrott by Hull's interest in their winger Pablo Garcia whom is valued around £7m.

Boro cancel Dieng's contract

Middlesbrough goalkeeper Seny Dieng has had his contract terminated by mutual consent. Dieng saw a loan move to Feyenoord fall through in January.

The 31-year-old has now linked up with Greek side Atromitos.

Vicario joins Juventus on loan

Tottenham have confirmed that goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has joined Juventus on an initial loan.

The deal includes an option to buy for £8.5m (€10m).

The 29-year-old travelled to Turin yesterday after talks accelerated on Sunday once Juventus opted against signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

Tottenham goalkeeper Vicario has joined Juventus on loan

West Ham finalise move for Piroe

West Ham are finalising forward Joel Piroe's arrival from Leeds United as misfit striker Niclas Fullkrug joins Werder Bremen on a season's loan.

The 33-year-old Germany international, who joined the Hammers for £27m from Borussia Dortmund in August 2024, scored three goals in 11 Premier League starts but spent the second half of last season on loan at AC Milan.

Fullkrug, a German international, returns to Werder for a third spell having also started his career with the Bundesliga club.

Gozo remains a goer

Zavier Gozo’s £11million move from Real Salt Lake to Crystal Palace is being held up by Major League Soccer paperwork.

Palace agreed the move with Real Salt Lake more than 10 days ago but all MLS players are employed by the league, meaning transfers are centrally scrutinised and controlled.

Every deal must be approved by MLS, which assesses the terms before a transfer can be finalised, making delays commonplace.

Gozo has already completed his medical and Palace remain confident of completing the transfer.

The 21-year-old attacker plays in the same position as Romain Esse, who had been due to leave for Club Brugge. That move has since fallen through. However, the collapse of Esse’s transfer has no impact on Gozo’s move to Selhurst Park.

BOBBY MANZI

Toffees chief pleads calm on right-back search

Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear is confident the club will sign a right-back but admits it will not be completed before the season opener against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Speaking to BBC Radio Merseyside, Kinnear said: 'I don’t think we are in a bad position on that.

'The players we thought we had the option of are still available for us, I don’t think they will be there for Crystal Palace, which was the objective.

'I’m confident that we’ll bring a right back in. It’s a position we’ve needed. I think Jake (O’Brien) has done a sterling job for us in that position.

'It was something that we were trying to do last summer and didn’t feel that we could get the quality in.

'So a right-back was top priority in the window, we would have liked to have got it done earlier.

'I understand the fans' frustrations; I understand how they see it as being critical.

'Even the Prime Minister chipped in to give us some helpful direction. So it’s reached a level of national importance.

'So we are working hard to bring one in and I’m sure we will. I’m sure it will be an improvement, and it will round off the squad nicely.'

Everton have looked at Palace's Daniel Munoz though Moyes regards him more as a wing-back. They enquired about Fulham's Timothy Castagne and had a bid rejected for Celtic's Alistair Johnston who picked up an injury.

Others such as Guela Doue at Strasbourg are considered too expensive while they have been offered Aston Villa target Aaron Wan-Bissaka but said no and, similarly, are not pursuing Burnley's Kyle Walker, so far.

Moyes has admitted they may have to revert to another option if they can't get their prime target.

Newcastle complete Dedic deal

Newcastle United have signed Bosnia and Herzegovina international Amar Dedic from Benfica for £29.5million on a five-year deal.

Newcastle United have signed Bosnia and Herzegovina international Amar Dedic from Benfica for £29.5million on a five-year deal.

The 24-year-old full-back becomes the sixth senior addition of the summer and will wear the No 37 shirt at St James' Park.

Dedic, who can operate on either flank, previously worked with Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle at Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering.

He made 95 appearances for Salzburg before spells with Marseille and Benfica, where he featured against Newcastle in last season's Champions League.

Newcastle United have completed the signing of full back Amar Dedic

Dedic has won 31 caps for Bosnia and Herzegovina and played at this summer's World Cup.

'Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again,' he said.

'Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started.'

Owls target Anfield youngster

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is a prime target for Sheffield Wednesday on loan.

The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season and has attracted varied interest from the likes of Wolfsburg and Bristol City.

However, League On Wednesday are emerging as strong favourites for his signature with Liverpool keen to see him get regular game time in a competitive division.

Liverpool youngster Kieran Morrison, 19, is a prime target for Sheffield Wednesday

Morrison can play centrally in attacking midfield as well as wide. He joined Liverpool from Manchester United's academy and was called up to the Northern Irish senior squad for the first time, ahead of their World Cup qualifying play-off against Italy in March. He made his senior debut in June, playing the first half of a 1–0 friendly win over Guinea.

Liverpool are continuing negotiations for Paris St Germain winger Bradley Barcola but, as it stands, Liverpool are unlikely to pursue interest in his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye despite exploratory talks.

Fulham monitor Brazilian defender Natan

Fulham have asked about Real Betis centre back Natan.

The Brazilian joined Betis from Napoli last summer for £7.5m and has attracted interest from other Premier League sides in recent weeks.

The 25-year-old is one of a number of options being considered by the Cottagers.

And elsewhere...

Aston Villa have agreed to loan right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic to Rangers with an obligation to buy for £3.5m.

Celtic also hold an interest in the Serbian international but he is expected for a medical at Ibrox later today.

Wolves are exploring a move for Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry. Rangers had a £7.5m bid rejected this week for the £10m-rated 21-year-old.

Brighton have been exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez.

Middlesbrough goalkeeper Seny Dieng has had his contract terminated by mutual consent.

Dieng saw a loan move to Feyenoord fall through in January. The 31-year-old has now linked up with Greek side Atromitos.

MONDAY: Liverpool unlikely to pursue PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye

SUNDAY: Juventus reopen talks for Spurs keeper Vicario

SATURDAY: Aston Villa in talks with Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki

FRIDAY: Djed Spence completes £30million move to Inter Milan

THURSDAY: Chelsea waiting for Fernandez bid

WEDNESDAY: Man United target Carlos Baleba on Newcastle's radar

TUESDAY: Roy Keane's son-in-law linked with move to Portugal
